ki-27_otsu: Nakajima's Type 97 Fighter of 1937 was the Japanese Army's first monoplane fighter, and 3,368 were built before the Ki-43 took over its frontline role in 1942. In the game it lives at low level: below about 1,000 m few comparable fighters can stay with it in a turn. Only two 7.7 mm guns and thin protection make it a weak interceptor, so it is better suited to covering friendly bombers and flying boats than to chasing targets down. It arrived in Update 1.43.
ki-27_otsu_china: Nakajima's Ki-27 (Allied codename "Nate") ended up with both sides of China's armed forces; the Nationalists found little use for it as a fighter, while the Communists put captured examples to work training pilots and engineers. Its flight model matches the Japanese version, so it turns superbly, but anything with a stronger engine or a height advantage is a real danger. It does best against enemies already dragged down low, either finishing them or crippling them for an assist. It came with the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
ki-27_otsu_ep: A Ki-27 otsu in the colours of the 4th Sentai at Tachiarai Air Base in Fukuoka, Kyūshū, a site that became an Army flight school in 1940 and prepared new Army pilots for combat over Asia. It sums up the Japanese air tree's priorities: superb manoeuvrability comes first, while protection is middling and the guns are underwhelming. It was added in the "Starfighters" update.
ki-45_hei: The third production model of the Ki-45 two-seat fighter went back to a 20 mm belly cannon after the disappointing Otsu and swapped the twin nose 12.7 mm guns for a drum-fed 37 mm Ho-203, settling the type's role as a bomber interceptor able to climb to their altitude. Its combined 20 mm and 37 mm burst is the hardest-hitting of the Ki-45 family, and it handles much like the cannon-armed Kai-Kō. The 37 mm empties quickly, though, so short, deliberate bursts matter. It was introduced in Update 1.31.
ki-45_hei_tei_china: Assembled from three captured Ki-45s of the Hei and Tei variants, this single aircraft was rebuilt by Communist forces in north-eastern China after WWII for evaluation and instruction, and never served as a real combatant; the Chinese simply called it a "heavy fighter". It pairs the Hei's fuselage 20 mm Ho-3 with the Tei's two upward-firing 20 mm Ho-5s, so no other Ki-45 in the game carries as much firepower, though it has no ordnance. Agile for a twin-engined fighter, it is a strong bomber hunter, but its small ammunition supply leaves it struggling against fighters. It arrived in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack" as a Golden Eagles purchase.
ki-45_ko: The Kai-Kō was the first production Ki-45, a twin-seat, general-purpose fighter Kawasaki built in parallel with the Ki-43 and Ki-44; early prototypes with Ha-25 engines lacked power, so the "Kai" re-engined it with Ha-102s. Armed with two nose 12.7 mm guns and a ventral 20 mm cannon, it carries the most forward-firing ammunition of any Ki-45. It is built for boom-and-zoom: climb and roll rate are only average, so gentle climbs and fast diving passes work better than turning. It came in Update 1.31.
ki-45_otsu: For the Kai-Otsu, the Ki-45's 20 mm cannon gave way to a Type 94 37 mm tank gun, the same weapon as the Ha-Go's, which the rear crewman had to reload by hand one round at a time. That makes it the awkward member of the family: the 37 mm carries little ammunition, fires slowly and drops sharply thanks to its short barrel, and even its APHE round penetrates poorly. In practice it flies like a heavy-cannon attacker without the big gun's payoff. It was introduced in Update 1.31.
ki-45_tei: The last Ki-45 production model borrowed the Navy J1N's idea of oblique Schräge Musik cannons, fitting two upward-firing 20 mm Ho-5s in place of the belly gun; production Tei aircraft also deleted the rear gunner. The in-game model is really a Kai-Hei with Tei armament, so the gunner remains. Firing the oblique guns needs a separate view keybind, and the method is to slide in beneath a bomber at matched speed and shoot from outside its gunners' arcs. Uniquely among Ki-45s, it can also carry ordnance, two 250 kg bombs. It arrived in Update 1.31.
ki-49_1: The Ki-49-I, the opening model of this Japanese bomber family in War Thunder, has been in the game since the open beta ahead of Update 1.27. It is quick in level flight, well protected from behind and, thanks to very large elevators, more agile than its size suggests; it was also the first Japanese bomber with substantial armour. That makes it flexible in air battles, able to bomb from low level or hit bases, and its speed means frequent trips to rearm can make up for a modest payload.
ki-49_2a: Japan's Ki-49 medium bomber was designed after Ki-21 operations showed that unescorted daylight raids needed far more armour and defensive guns; the IIa added stronger Ha-109 engines in place of the Ha-41s, self-sealing tanks and better armour. In the game it is a low-level attacker of pillboxes, tanks and similar ground targets, held back by a small bomb load but unusually nimble for a bomber. Its armour and guns, the dorsal 20 mm cannon above all, help drive off fighters. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
ki-49_2b: A Japanese medium bomber in the game since the open beta (before Update 1.27), the Ki-49-IIb works best low down against pillboxes, tanks and other ground targets. Its total bomb load is small, but it turns well enough to circle over a target area and unload quickly, something big bombers such as the G8N1 Renzan struggle with. The 4 x 250 kg option suits tanks, pillboxes, bases and small ships.
ki-49_2b_late: Another Japanese bomber present since the open beta before Update 1.27, the Ki-49-IIb/L is meant for low-level strikes on ground targets such as tanks, pillboxes and small ships. It cannot carry much in total, but it is agile for its class and can keep circling over a target to drop everything in quick succession, unlike large, slow-turning heavies such as the G8N1. Against tanks, pillboxes or light ships, the four 250 kg bomb load is the recommended choice.
ki-83: Tomio Kubo's team, creators of the Ki-46, designed the Ki-83 to a 1943 Army requirement for a long-range heavy fighter, using two turbocharged 2,200 hp engines; in testing it reached 9,750 m in under ten minutes. Four prototypes flew, bombing raids stalled the programme, and the last survivor went to the US and was probably scrapped. In the game no propeller-driven aircraft out-climbs it; it also handles well and packs two 30 mm and two 20 mm nose cannons with plenty of ammunition. Its two 50 kg bombs are not worth the performance cost. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
ki-96: Kawasaki built the Ki-96 privately in 1942 as a bigger-engined follow-on to its Ki-45; the Army asked for it as a single-seater, then went back to wanting two seats and cancelled it, though its wings and tail lived on in the Ki-102. The game's version follows the later single-seat prototypes, armed with a 37 mm Ho-203 and two 20 mm Ho-5s in the nose. It shreds bombers from oblique angles, suits boom-and-zoom, and is nimble enough to dogfight single-engined fighters, but ammunition runs short quickly. It was added in Update 1.35.
ki_100_2: Kawasaki began the Ki-100-II in March 1945 as a high-altitude interceptor against B-29 formations, giving its Ha-112-II Ru engine a turbocharger and water-methanol injection; only three prototypes were completed before Japan's defeat. Compared with the standard Ki-100 it gives up speed and agility at low and medium heights in exchange for strong performance at 8–10 km, where few fights take place. Even so, it stays well rounded, and its nose armament is heavy by Japanese standards, enough for both fighters and four-engined bombers. It came in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
ki_100_early: Developed from the Ki-61-II by fitting a Ha-112-2 radial, the Ki-100 climbed faster and let Japan contest Allied raids on the home islands in 1945. Its default camouflage carries the markings of the 59th Sentai, a unit that fought in China and then from Java to New Guinea before returning to defend northern Kyushu, ending the war on Ki-100s. In the game it carries over the Ki-61's all-round balance of speed, dive, climb, turning and firepower: nothing stands out, but it gives the pilot plenty of ways to fight. It was introduced in Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
ki_102_otsu: Known informally as the Type 4 Assault Aircraft, the Ki-102 otsu was a twin-engined, two-seat attacker derived from the Ki-45 that entered service in 1944; it saw little action beyond Okinawa and was mostly held back for home defence. It carries a 57 mm nose cannon, two ventral 20 mm cannons and a rear 12.7 mm gun. It can work as a ground attacker against light and soft targets or as an improvised bomber hunter; the 57 mm hits hard but is inaccurate, so single shots work better than bursts. It arrived in Update 1.35.
ki_108: Derived from the Ki-96 and Ki-102, the Ki-108 Kai was a heavy fighter prototype with a pressurised cockpit, meant to reach B-29s at altitude on turbosupercharged Ha-112-II Ru radials; just four were built and none fought. In the game it pairs a 37 mm nose cannon and two 20 mm chin guns with solid climb and fair agility, but its engines are easily knocked out. It is best used on bombers, attacking head-on or from the flank to stay clear of their gunners, and should avoid even fights with fighters, as it can neither out-turn nor outrun them. It was added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
ki_109: Mitsubishi's Ki-67 bomber was converted into the Ki-109 interceptor to counter the US high-altitude raids on Japan, gaining an adapted 75 mm anti-aircraft gun and losing every defensive position except the tail turret. The big gun can bring down bombers and, with a clean hit, knock out tanks, but it is no tool for agile fighters or other fast-moving targets. With such weak defensive fire, fighters are best avoided altogether. It joined the game in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ki_10_1: Takeo Doi, Richard Vogt's successor as Kawasaki's chief designer, drew up the Ki-10, a V-12-powered biplane that beat Nakajima's monoplane Ki-11 for an Army contract because it turned better. Entering service in 1937, it fought in China and South-east Asia and was the Army's last biplane fighter. In the game it is swifter than rival biplanes and gains height more easily, yet it is lightly armed and poorly protected, with two slow-firing 7.7 mm guns best loaded with stealth belts. Its place is low-level turning fights with biplanes and slow monoplanes, aiming at wings and leaving bombers alone. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_10_1_commander: A Ki-10-I in the markings of the 1st Hiko Sentai, the Japanese Army Air Service's first flying unit, formed on 5 July 1938; it flew the type until May 1942 before converting to the Ki-27, after which the Ki-10 went to training and secondary roles. Performance matches the other Ki-10s: good turning, reasonable climb and low speed, with little armour and light 7.7 mm armament that is outclassed against bombers or armoured aircraft. It does best turning with biplanes and slow monoplanes at low altitude, with team support. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_10_2: Kawasaki's Ki-10-II improved on the first model by fitting a more powerful engine under a redesigned cowling, plus an enlarged rudder and reinforced undercarriage, lifting top speed from 400 to 430 km/h and climb from 11.7 to 13.3 m/s. In the game it plays almost like the Ki-10-I: a good low-altitude turner with more speed and climb than rival biplanes, but with flimsy protection and two slow-firing 7.7 mm guns, for which stealth belts are the pick. Its prey is other biplanes and slow monoplanes; armoured targets and bombers are best left to others. It has been available since the open beta.
ki_10_2_commander: Painted for the 77th Hiko Sentai, formed in July 1938 out of the 8th Daitai, this Ki-10-II wears the unit's coloured tail field with thin stripes and twin "seagull" arrowheads that read as "77". The unit supported ground offensives in China and kept flying Ki-10s even after Soviet-supplied I-15s and I-16s outclassed them. It handles like the standard Ki-10-II, turning well at low level with weak guns and little armour. It has been in the game since the open beta but can no longer be obtained; only players who got it before its removal still have it.
ki_21_1hei: The Ki-21-Ic, third production version of the Type 97 Heavy Bomber, kept the Ib's revised control surfaces and added extra machine guns and bigger fuel tanks for range. It looks like any other Ki-21, but its defensive firepower is three times greater, with two more guns on each side and a remotely operated tail gun that punishes fighters sitting directly behind. It first appeared in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai" as a 2016 Winter Holiday event reward, and was later a Warbond battle trophy from Battle Pass Season I to Season IV.
ki_21_1ko: The Ki-21, or Type 97 Heavy Bomber, was designed around speed and range rather than armour or payload, the idea being to hit enemy airfields before their fighters could take off and to outrun interceptors; the Ia was its first production model, and it lost effectiveness as the war went on. In the game it is a nimble low-level bomber with a small total load, good against pillboxes, tanks, destroyers and cargo ships. Twenty 50 kg bombs suit scattered ground targets and two 500 kg bombs suit bases, while the light turrets favour higher altitudes. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
ki_32: Designed in 1936 to replace the Kawasaki Ki-3, the Ki-32 light bomber was required to reach 400 km/h, carry 450 kg of bombs and dive at 60 degrees; 854 were produced up to 1940, and it left frontline service in December 1941. It opens the Japanese dive-bomber line, and its high-altitude spawn lets it reach bases before fighters can climb to it despite a low top speed. It turns well enough to hold its own against contemporary monoplanes with its single wing gun, while twin rear 7.7 mm guns give solid protection from low-rank attackers. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
ki_43_1: First production model of Nakajima's Hayabusa, the Ki-43-I grew out of the Ki-27 with more speed and climb in mind; it first flew on 12 December 1938, but poor pilot feedback delayed adoption until early 1941, and roughly 750 were built in 1941–42 before the Ki-43-II took over. While the Navy's Zero took the headlines, the Hayabusa carried much of the Army's air war. In the game it shows the typical Japanese trade-off: outstanding agility, paid for with low top speed and poor survivability, and few aircraft are better at close turning fights. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
ki_43_2: Nakajima reworked the Ki-43 in 1942 to fix its fragile wing, low speed and inability to carry bombs: the Ki-43-II got a stronger Ha-115 engine, a three-bladed propeller, a reinforced wing with racks for bombs or drop tanks, a pilot backplate and protected fuel tanks. About 5,000 were built and served across the Pacific. In the game the gains are modest but meaningful: slightly higher speed, a wing that tolerates hard manoeuvres at almost any speed, and two bombs for mixed battles, all while remaining one of the most agile aircraft around. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_43_3_ko: Chinese forces captured Ki-43s (Allied codename "Oscar") more than once: a Ki-43-Ic was taken in April 1942, the Nationalist air force flew surviving examples around Nanjing until 1946, and the Communists turned eight into trainers. This Ki-43-III ko has an uprated engine for better diving speed. Its two 12.7 mm nose guns remain a weak armament, but the airframe keeps the Hayabusa's superb agility, even against Japanese opponents. It joined the game with the Chinese tech tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
ki_43_3_otsu: A Japanese Army Hayabusa variant, the Ki-43-III otsu is light and extremely agile, with excellent climb and roll rates, but fragile enough that even rifle-calibre hits can do real harm. Its key change from the Ki-43-II is armament: two 20 mm Ho-5 cannons replace the 12.7 mm Ho-103s, giving it the punch to destroy most opponents. With just 300 rounds, short bursts from 200–500 m are the way to use them, and careful use of combat flaps and throttle lets it win most low and mid-altitude turning fights. It arrived in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
ki_44_1: Nakajima designed the Ki-44 alongside the light Ki-43 and twin-engined Ki-45 as a faster, cannon-armed answer to fighters like the Bf 109 and Spitfire; it ended up lighter than a Bf 109 and in some respects bettered an imported Bf 109 E-7, though visibility was poor and landing speed high. Service began in 1941, yet many experienced pilots resented giving up agility for speed. In the game it is still reasonably nimble, yet less so than the Ki-43 or A6M, so it works best diving on targets and climbing away to repeat the attack.
ki_44_1_ep: Ki-44-I 'Red 34' flew with the 47th Sentai, which began as the independent 47th Chutai, the first unit to receive the Ki-44; recalled from Indochina after the 1942 Doolittle Raid, it became a Sentai in 1943 and defended the homeland from Narimasu against B-29s, later adding a ramming "Shinten" flight and some Ki-84s. In the game the Ki-44 can finally trade blows with Western fighters on armament and mobility. It cannot turn with the Ki-43 or A6M, so boom-and-zoom suits it, but it is faster than those Japanese stablemates. It came in the "Starfighters" update.
ki_44_2_hei: The final standard Ki-44 model and the most produced, the IIc carried four 12.7 mm guns and a Type 100 optical sight, and many earlier aircraft were upgraded to match. Disliked by many pilots and overtaken by the Ki-84, it ended up mainly defending the home islands. The default scheme is that of the 70th Sentai, a B-29 interceptor unit whose pilots were readying for the Ki-200 when the war ended. In the game its four HE-loaded 12.7 mm guns hit hard, but opponents are tougher too, so it relies on a height advantage and quick kills before enemies can run it down. It arrived in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
ki_44_2_hei_china: China's Ki-44-II hei flies exactly like the Japanese original and arrived with Update 1.91 "Night Vision". The "Shoki" name refers to Zhong Kui, a fearsome and famously ugly figure of Chinese mythology, which suits a squat, stubby fighter wearing weathered paint in Chinese service. Looks aside, it has outstanding performance for its rank, built around speed and climb while keeping good agility by non-Japanese standards, and pilots who know the CW-21 will find its tactics familiar.
ki_44_2_otsu: The Ki-44-IIb paired an improved engine and nose 12.7 mm guns with optional 40 mm wing cannons meant for American bombers, though they only worked at near-ramming range with little ammunition, and some were swapped for 12.7 mm guns; that close-in approach later fed into the Army's Shinten ramming units. In the game the 40 mm shells are devastating but painfully slow, so they are best saved for bombers and delivered from close range at speed; the strong engine gets it to altitude quickly. Once they are gone, the HE-loaded 12.7 mm guns make it a capable boom-and-zoom fighter. It arrived in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
ki_48_2_otsu: In the invasion of China, Japan's Ki-48 light bomber went after supply lines and infrastructure early in the war, and its crews valued the speed that let it outrun fighters. This Ki-48-II otsu was a gift reward from the 2023 Tokushu Heiki event, added in the "Sons of Attila" update, and it is the only propeller aircraft in the game able to carry a guided missile: the Ki-148, whose 130 kg TNT warhead wrecks the lightly armoured tanks it meets. Speed lets it get out of trouble, and two rear gunners discourage pursuers.
ki_61_1a_hei: Kawasaki's Ki-61-I hei, built from September 1943 to July 1944 alongside the otsu, replaced the wing machine guns with imported German MG 151/20 cannons, a stopgap while Japan's own 20 mm guns lagged; Kawasaki staff nicknamed it "Type Ma" after Mauser. The extra weight cost some performance. In the game it is the best-armed Ki-61-I, and the two 20 mm cannons kill fighters and bombers far more reliably than the kō and otsu's machine guns. It keeps the family's stability, strong dive and decent mid-altitude speed, and suits energy tactics and short, decisive engagements. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_61_1a_hei_ep: Takeichi Tada of the 78th Sentai flew this Ki-61-I hei. Formed in Manchuria in 1942 on Ki-27s, the unit converted to the Ki-61 in Japan, went to Rabaul in June 1943, scored the type's first aerial victory and was effectively wiped out by July 1944. In the game it turns well but is barely faster than early Zeros, though it accelerates and holds energy nicely, rather like a Bf 109 G-6. Its MG 151s with Minengeschoß shells and HE-loaded 12.7 mm guns are lethal, effective flaps help force overshoots, and it can carry bombs, of which 250 kg is the best choice. It came in the "Starfighters" update.
ki_61_1a_ko: Takeo Doi designed the Ki-61 to a 1940 Army requirement, building it around a licence-built DB 601 (Ha-40) with a sturdy metal airframe, self-sealing tanks and armour, and favouring hit-and-run tactics; it became Japan's only mass-produced fighter with a liquid-cooled inline engine. The first model, the kō, mixed two 12.7 mm and two 7.7 mm guns because heavy guns were in short supply, and unreliable engines dogged its service from 1943. In the game it is balanced rather than ultra-agile, faster than most Japanese contemporaries but average by other nations' standards, and the 7.7 mm guns mainly a fallback. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_61_1a_otsu: The second Ki-61 production model, built from September 1943 to April 1944, got the armament originally planned: four 12.7 mm Ho-103s, with the wing 7.7 mm guns gone. Lessons from the kō also brought better-protected fuel and extra armour for the pilot, and the tailwheel was fixed to ease production. In the game it keeps the Ki-61's balance of speed, stable mid-altitude handling and durability, while the four heavy machine guns give steadier hitting power than its predecessor. Climb and turn are not its strengths, so it works best as an energy fighter that picks its moments. It has been in the game since the open beta.
ki_61_1a_otsu_china: Flown in Chinese colours, this Ki-61-I otsu arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision". Compared with the Zero, the Ki-61 is faster, climbs better and handles better at speed, though it is less agile; its inline engine and gun layout give it a Bf 109-like look. In the game its climb is better than the stat card suggests, letting it reach heights few opponents can match and choose its fights, diving in and zooming away rather than turning. Its four 12.7 mm Ho-103s carry plenty of ammunition but lack punch and velocity, so close range and good lead are essential.
ki_61_1a_otsu_usa: An American-captured example of the Ki-61-I otsu, this premium has been in the game since the open beta. Like the Japanese version it carries four 12.7 mm Ho-103 guns with ample ammunition, and it outpaces, out-climbs and outguns the earlier Ki-43. Its real asset is climb, which is stronger than the stat card implies and lets it sit above most opponents and decide when to engage. It plays as an energy fighter: dive on a target, and if it survives, zoom back up out of reach of its guns for another pass.
ki_61_1a_tei: When imported MG 151 cannons ran out, the Ki-61-I tei (built January 1944 to January 1945) switched to two domestic 20 mm Ho-5s in the nose, which needed a longer nose, wings moved forward, rear ballast and a smaller main tank, and cost even more performance. Ha-140 engine delays kept it in production, making it the most numerous Ki-61. In the game it is a touch heavier and less agile than earlier Ki-61s, but the centreline cannons are accurate and free of convergence worries. It is best flown as an energy fighter, diving in for a decisive burst and extending away. It was introduced in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
ki_61_2_early: The Ki-61-II Kai was meant to cap the Ki-61 line with the DB 605-derived Ha-140, but the engine was so unreliable that many finished airframes sat engineless until they became Ki-100s. Its armament followed the Ki-61-I tei, with 12.7 mm guns kept in the wings, and later aircraft gained a teardrop canopy, which is why historians split the type into kō and otsu. In the game reliability is no issue, yet added weight eats most of the extra power, leaving it only slightly better than the tei; the real gain is 200 rounds per Ho-5 cannon instead of 120. It came in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
ki_67_1_ko: Designed to replace the Ki-49, the Ki-67 was built to survive, with armour and self-sealing tanks, while remaining agile enough to dive-bomb; it reached units in October 1944 and spawned variants such as the Ki-109 interceptor, but only 767 were completed. The Ko is the main production model with a single tail gun. In the game it is fast, tough and well defended, carries a wide choice of bombs and torpedoes, and is at its best attacking pillboxes and other individual ground targets rather than bases. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ki_67_1_otsu: The Ki-67-I otsu is the later main production model of the Type 4 Heavy Bomber, which was intended to succeed the Ki-49 and combined armour and sealed tanks with enough agility for dive attacks; 767 Ki-67s of all versions were finished amid Allied raids. Its distinguishing feature is a twin-gun tail position, giving it stronger rear defence than the Ko. In the game it is quick and hard to bring down, with bombs or torpedoes for almost any role, though its load is better spent on pillboxes and other frontline targets than on bases. It joined the game in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ki_84_hei: Nakajima built the Ki-84 to succeed its Ki-43, keeping the agility while adding armour, heavier guns and better climb; it flew in April 1943, entered mass production in April 1944, and 3,514 of all versions were made. The Hei paired two 30 mm Ho-155s with two 20 mm Ho-5s. In the game it keeps the climb, smooth handling and agility of earlier Ki-84s, but it stiffens up at high speed, the heavy guns are hard to use well, and it turns worse than other Japanese fighters. Against tougher opposition its edge is smaller than its predecessors'. It was added in Update 1.37.
ki_84_ko: Nakajima's Ki-84 was ordered in 1942 to replace the Ki-43, fixing its weak guns, thin protection and climb with a pilot backplate, armoured glass, heavy machine guns and two 20 mm cannons. It first flew in April 1943, and the Ko, the first and most numerous production model, entered mass production in April 1944; 3,514 Ki-84s of all kinds were built, some ending up in China. In the game it climbs superbly and handles well, but its controls stiffen at high speed, its armament is light and other Japanese fighters out-turn it. It was introduced in Update 1.37.
ki_84_ko_china: Known as Hayate ("Gale") in Japanese service and "Frank" to the Allies, the Ki-84 first saw combat over mainland China defending Japanese assets from US and Nationalist bombers; after the 1945 surrender the Nationalist air force took over scattered examples until American aircraft arrived, while the Communists used them for ground attack and training before the PLAAF formed in 1949. It performs exactly like the Japanese Ko: a well-rounded fighter that climbs quickly for energy tactics and can still turn when needed, though its guns struggle against armoured bombers and attackers. It arrived in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack" as a Golden Eagles premium.
ki_84_otsu: Following the Ko into limited production, the Ki-84 Otsu replaced the mixed armament with four 20 mm Ho-5 cannons; the type had been commissioned in 1942 to succeed the Ki-43 with better guns, armour and climb, and 3,514 Ki-84s of all variants were built by the war's end. In the game the stronger guns come with the same strengths as before, excellent climb, lively performance and good handling, and the same flaws: the controls stiffen at high speed and other Japanese fighters out-turn it. It was introduced in Update 1.37.
ki_87: Built to counter B-29 raids, the Ki-87 used a turbo-supercharged Ha-44-12 radial for performance above 10,000 m, along with a pressurised cockpit and four-bladed propeller; development from 1942 was slowed by technical problems and shortages, and only one prototype flew, in April 1945. In the game it is a heavily armed super-prop whose two 30 mm and two 20 mm cannons tear bombers apart, and it is strongest high up and in dives. It turns and rolls sluggishly, overheats on WEP and benefits from manual engine control. Added as a pack in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters", it later returned as a Golden Eagles premium.
ki_93_1_ko: Begun in 1941 at the Army Aerotechnical Research Institute and refined at the Tachikawa arsenal, the Ki-93 was a twin-engined heavy fighter and attacker with two Ha-214 radials and heavy armour around the crew. The Ko bomber-interceptor flew on 8 April 1945, was damaged landing and then destroyed in an American raid. In the game its 57 mm Ho-402 can wreck bombers with one HE hit and its APHE pierces about 70 mm of armour, while two 20 mm Ho-5s add burst mass. Steel crew plates of 12 mm, a small fuel tank and good high-altitude performance round it out. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
ki_94_2: Tachikawa's Ki-94-II was a pressurised single-seat interceptor meant for high-flying B-29s, a simpler successor to the rejected twin-boom Ki-94-I, with a Ha-219 (Ha-44) engine and four wing cannons; two prototypes were built and neither flew before the war ended. In the game its strong engine, long wings and responsive elevator are offset by poor climb and slow engine response. It suits boom-and-zoom from above and hit-and-run at equal height; Spitfires out-turn it, though careful use of flaps and throttle can beat P-47s and P-51Ds. Its fuel tanks are vulnerable. It was an Operation S.U.M.M.E.R. 2017 event reward in Update 1.69.
kitsuka: Japan's first jet, Nakajima's Kikka was a Navy attack aircraft meant to hit US warships with bombs at speed; though inspired by German progress, it was a domestic design, simplified so unskilled labour could mass-produce it. Only two prototypes were tested before the war ended. In the game it is a fast fighter-bomber whose single 30 mm gains a second cannon through the 'otsu' modification. Speed is its main advantage, so heavy bomb loads of up to 800 kg are best kept for ground and naval strikes, made in fast diving runs to slip past anti-aircraft fire. It came in Update 1.43.
kor_1: The Beriev KOR-1 (later Be-2) was a two-seat, open-cockpit reconnaissance floatplane with an M-25 radial, built to replace the He 55 biplane; it was troublesome and hard to handle, only 12 were made, and they flew from shore bases rather than ships before retiring in 1942. In the game it serves as the catapult aircraft of Kirov-class cruisers and, with two nose ShKAS and one defensive ShKAS, is roughly comparable to an I-153 in firepower and handling. Two 100 kg FAB-100sv bombs give it a way to hurt coastal vessels. It was added in the "Winged Lions" update.
kor_2: Beriev's bureau designed the KOR-2 (Be-4) shipborne flying boat from 1938 because the KOR-1 handled poorly and was built too slowly. The first aircraft was finished at Savelovo in August 1941 before production moved to Omsk and, from 1944, Krasnoyarsk; they flew coastal reconnaissance, convoy escort and anti-submarine patrols in the Black Sea and were catapulted from Project 26 cruisers. In the game it is the catapult scout for Soviet ships, with a single defensive ShKAS and one forward ShKAS, but its two 100 kg bombs can threaten small boats. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
l_39za: The L-39 Albatros was a Czechoslovak jet trainer from Letňany, developed in 1968 to replace the L-29; the L-39ZA, produced from 1980, added a reinforced wing and a ventral pod with a GSh-23L twin-barrel 23 mm cannon. Reliable, easy to maintain and able to use dirt strips, it went to more than 30 countries and many still fly. In the game it handles responsively even at top speed, has an air brake and a wide range of stores, but slow acceleration, little cannon ammunition and no ballistic computer make it hard work in air and mixed battles. It joined the Soviet tree in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
l_39za_art_thailand: Thailand's air force ordered the L-39ZA/ART, an L-39ZA with Elbit electronics, in the early 1990s: 36 arrived by October 1993 and four more by 1997. The 401st and 411th Squadrons trained on them for fighter, attack and search-and-rescue work until the 401st switched to T-50THs in 2018 and the 411th retired its last ones in March 2021. It sits in the Japanese air tree, handling responsively with decent manoeuvrability and a useful selection of stores, but it accelerates poorly and is slow overall. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
la-11: The La-11 grew out of the La-9 as the La-130 and then La-9M, gaining fuel and weight before certification in 1947; jets made it obsolete by 1951, and after limited combat it mostly trained pilots, also serving North Korea and China. In the game the long-range La-11 is heavier than the La-9 but flies almost identically on light fuel loads, and its engine does best below about 4,000 m. Three NS-23 cannons reliably down fighters, bombers and heavy fighters. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai", it left the store after the 2018 Summer Sale and returned briefly in 2021.
la-11_china: Among the last piston fighters ever built, the La-11 was a long-range escort fighter that China's air force flew alongside the La-9 until jets arrived; it scored the PLAAF's first propeller-versus-jet kill but was also involved in shooting down a civil airliner in the mid-1950s, and survivors flew for two more decades until spares ran out. In the game it is a capable interceptor, fast and well armed enough to chase off American and British fighters, though it has one 23 mm cannon fewer than the La-9. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
la-15: Lavochkin's Project 52, inspired by captured plans for the unbuilt German Ta 183, yielded two jets; the one with a copied Derwent (the RD-500) became the La-15, entering service in 1949, and 235 were built before supersonic types pushed it out in 1953. In the game its engine is far stronger than its wings, which can fail even in level flight, so it fights best at low to medium speed, where its thrust lets it turn briefly, out-accelerate rivals or climb to catch bombers. Few opponents can follow it in a straight-line escape, though missile-armed jets such as the F9F-8 negate that. It arrived in Update 1.39.
la-5_type37_early: The first La-5 (type 37) married a 1,700 hp M-82A radial to two 20 mm ShVAK cannons and handled much like a Bf 109 F; early aircraft suffered from cockpit heat, fumes and poor canopies, and 1,021 were built after it entered service in 1942, though it still needed work to match the Bf 109 G and Fw 190. In the game it is an energy fighter: sluggish at low speed and prone to stiffening controls when fast, it does best patrolling around 2,000–3,000 m and diving on distracted or weaker opponents. The cannons are effective, but limited ammunition calls for restraint. It came in Update 1.35.
la-5_type39: The La-5F brought the M-82F engine, which could run continuously at boosted power, plus weight savings, a cut-down rear fuselage fairing, new radio, cockpit ventilation and bulletproof glass; it outperformed the La-5, notably at low level, and 4,150 were built by the end of 1943. In the game it flies much like the original La-5 with extra power. Its reinforced wings suit boom-and-zoom, though it is less at home in sustained energy fights, and its two 20 mm cannons deal well with fighters but can fall short against bombers and heavy twins. It was introduced in Update 1.35.
la-5fn: Built alongside the La-5F rather than after it, the La-5FN introduced the fuel-injected ASh-82FN, giving 1,850 hp for up to ten minutes; in trials against a Bf 109 G-2 it proved faster and more agile at low and medium altitude, which shaped Soviet tactics. Its twin 20 mm ShVAKs had 200 rounds each. As the final La-5 in the game, it takes the family's style further: accurate cannons, superb low-altitude performance and strong boom-and-zoom ability, now with the power to excel in low to medium altitude fights. It has been in the game since the open beta.
la-7: Lavochkin's La-7 refined the La-5 with a new metal airframe and much better performance; despite early gun and engine troubles it proved faster and nimbler, took on Bf 109s and Fw 190s with success, and was flown by the Soviet ace Ivan Kozhedub before the La-9 replaced it post-war. Planned triple 20 mm cannons fell through, so it kept the La-5's two ShVAKs. In the game it is a strong low to mid-altitude interceptor that can both boom-and-zoom and dogfight, ideally starting fights with an energy or height advantage, though a Spitfire will still out-turn it. It has been in the game since the open beta.
la-7_dolgushin: This La-7 wears the scheme flown from September 1944 by Sergei Dolgushin of the 156th IAP, a Hero of the Soviet Union credited with 15 solo and 8 shared victories. A flying-school classmate of Vasily Stalin, he downed two German aircraft on 22 June 1941, later served under Stalin's son in the 32nd GIAP and commanded the 156th until 1946. It flies exactly like the tech-tree La-7. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it left the store after the 2017 Victory Day sales and has returned only briefly since.
la-7b-20: The La-7 was meant to carry three B-20S 20 mm cannons, and 368 were built that way, a fit test pilots liked and nicknamed the "three-pointer", before reliability problems led to the La-5's twin ShVAKs being used instead. In the game the third gun makes every burst more destructive, but the extra weight blunts performance compared with the standard La-7, despite the same M-82FN engine, and each gun has less ammunition. It works best with boom-and-zoom, keeping dogfights below 4,000 m where the engine is strongest. It was introduced in Update 1.31.
la-9: Lavochkin's La-9 swapped the wooden construction of types like the La-7 for an all-metal airframe, with a pressurised cockpit to deal with heat, an ASh-82FN radial and four 23 mm NS-23 cannons; 1,882 were built up to 1949, serving the USSR, China and North Korea until jets took over. In the game it performs well, comfortable with boom-and-zoom or low-level fighting, and its engine is strongest below 4,000 m. The cannons hit very hard but ammunition is limited, so short bursts keep it in the fight for the whole match. It arrived in Update 1.37.
la-9_china: Already obsolete when it appeared in 1946, the La-9 was still a cheap way to build up an air force, and the newly formed PLAAF, with fewer than 20 mostly captured fighters, ordered 120 in August 1949. They flew in the Korean War before MiG-15bis jets displaced them into training and occasional attack duties against insurgents. In the game it matches the Soviet version, facing early jets with an air-cooled engine that weakens at height; when teammates drag enemies down low, its four 23 mm cannons can run them down and destroy them. It came with the first Chinese air tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
la_174: The La-174 is an early prototype of the La-15 from Lavochkin's Project 52, which produced a Derwent-powered version and a Nene-powered 174D; the Derwent one, built as the RD-500, went into production. Among the rarest jets in the game, it was available only during two Lavochkin birthday events, in 2014 and 2017, and required the La-15 to be researched first. Apart from minor performance differences and its paint, it flies like the La-15: enormous thrust for energy fights, but wings that tear off easily at speed, and missile-armed opponents in uptiers can cancel its speed advantage. It came in Update 1.39.
la_200_toriy: Designed in the late 1940s as a radar-equipped all-weather interceptor to guard key Soviet sites, the La-200 beat three competing designs but was overtaken by the more practical Yak-120 (Yak-25), and just a single prototype was completed. In the game it can exceed 1,000 km/h, enough to outrun most opponents, and at medium to high altitude it is very hard to catch while it delivers boom-and-zoom attacks with three N-37D cannons. Its great weakness is low-speed flight, where it becomes sluggish and unstable. It was added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
lagg-3-11: The 11th-series LaGG-3 introduced an M-105PA engine without a float-chamber carburettor, rails for six rockets or DZ-40 bomb racks, larger wheels and no outer-wing fuel tanks, cutting fuel to 260 kg. Of 6,528 LaGG-3s, around 700 belonged to the 11th and 23rd series, and the type fought on until the 1945 campaign against Japan. In the game it shares the family's strong guns and decent speed along with poor climb and agility, making dogfights hard work. Its underwing stores give it some use against ground targets, though heavy armour needs precise hits. It was introduced in Update 1.33.
lagg-3-23: Designed by OKB-301 (Lavochkin, Gorbunov and Gudkov), the LaGG-3 in its 23rd series differed from the 11th mainly in a slightly modified tail, and was built over the winter and spring of 1942. In the game it carries the family's heavy armament and decent speed, plus underwing weapons that allow ground attack, although armoured vehicles need very precise strikes. It flies a little better than the 11th series, yet it is still out-turned by many opponents and has a hard time in dogfights. It has been in the game since the open beta.
lagg-3-34: Replacing the hub-firing 20 mm ShVAK with a 37 mm NS-37 turned this LaGG-3 into a tank-buster in the manner of the later Yak-9T; 40 were sent to Stalingrad for trials in 1942, but the gun upset the balance and its recoil damaged engines, so development stopped. In the game it is an effective ground-attack aircraft that can still defend itself, filling the Yak-9T's role with performance closer to the early Yak-9. It arrived in Update 1.41.27 in a starter pack, was sold in premium packs until early 2019, and also appeared as a Warbond battle trophy prize.
lagg-3-35: Built at Tbilisi's Factory No. 31 from August 1942 to spring 1943, the 35th-series LaGG-3 gained automatic slats, a retractable tailwheel, a larger air intake and a pitot tube on the right wing to improve its aerodynamics; about 800 were made. In the game it keeps the family's punchy guns and decent speed, but it is not agile and has limited ammunition, so both dogfighting and ground attack demand accurate shooting and careful bomb drops. It has been in the game since the open beta.
lagg-3-4: One of the rarest aircraft in the game, the LaGG-3-4 was handed out only to developers and people who made significant contributions to War Thunder, and has been present since the open beta. It belongs to the M-105PA-engined group of LaGG-3s alongside the 8th, 11th and 23rd series, which differ only in small details and fly in much the same way. It is a fighter first and foremost: an average climb rate and a fragile engine make it a poor choice for hunting bombers.
lagg-3-66: The 66th series was the final and best-flying LaGG-3, with a lighter structure and 55 mm armoured glass among its improvements; around 1,000 were built at Tbilisi's Plant No. 31 between spring 1943 and July 1944. In the game it keeps the heavy armament of earlier series, while the thick windscreen protects the pilot in head-on passes and handling is noticeably better. German Bf 109s and similar types have the upper hand at height, but below about 3,000 m an experienced pilot can make it a dangerous opponent. It was introduced in Update 1.31.
lagg-3-8: From the 8th series onward, the LaGG-3 lost its 7.62 mm ShKAS machine guns, which cost it its firepower lead over the Yak-1 but saved weight without much loss of punch; up to 400 of this series were among 6,528 LaGG-3s built. In the game it has the usual LaGG traits, strong guns and fair speed but poor climb and turning. With no ShKAS and limited ShVAK and UBS ammunition, inaccurate pilots will struggle in dogfights, so every burst needs to count. It was introduced in Update 1.33.
lagg-i-301: Prototype of the LaGG-3, the I-301 used a wood-and-polymer structure and a 1,050 hp M-105P engine, first flying in March 1940 with an exceptionally powerful 23 mm PTB-23 cannon; extra wing tanks were later added to fix its short range. In the game it flies much like the LaGG-3-8, slightly faster than the LaGG-3-66, but outguns its relatives with the engine-mounted 23 mm plus two 12.7 mm and two 7.62 mm machine guns. Boom-and-zoom suits it, though the wing tanks catch fire easily and the engine overheats quickly. It was a 2014 Winter Holiday giveaway in Update 1.43.
lancaster_mk1: Avro's Lancaster began in 1940 as a fix for the troubled Manchester, replacing two unreliable Vultures with four Merlins and a longer wing to become a heavy bomber; its long, unbroken bomb bay could take huge loads, and 7,377 of all models were built. This B Mk I represents the initial production standard. In the game it carries up to about 6,500 kg, either fourteen 1,000 lb bombs or a single 12,000 lb "Blockbuster" that levels everything nearby. Weak defensive guns and a fragile airframe mean it relies on acceleration, agility for its size and a fast shallow dive to avoid fighters. It came in Update 1.43.
lancaster_mk3: Developed in parallel with the Mk I, the Lancaster B Mk III used Packard-built Merlins with pressure-injection carburettors, gaining a little speed but losing ceiling. Losses to German heavy fighters showed its four-gun .303 tail turret was too weak, so from late 1944 the twin .50 cal "Rose turret" was fitted. The in-game Mk III represents that late configuration; the heavier tail guns give it a real chance against attackers, but defence overall remains poor, so avoiding interceptors is still the best way to deliver its large payload. It has been in the game since the open beta.
lancaster_mr7_france: France's Aéronavale ordered 59 B.I and B.VII Lancasters converted into maritime patrol aircraft, delivered by Avro in 1952–53 as the last direct Lancaster variant; four squadrons flew them from France and New Caledonia until the mid-1960s. The French version differs from the British one: it still carries enough to destroy a base or carpet-bomb a large area, and adds a radar, but its defensive guns cover only the nose and tail, and it cannot take the 12,000 lb bomb, its largest being 1,000 lb with many smaller ones. It arrived in the "La Royale" update.
late_298d: Latécoère's 298 first flew in 1936 as the French Navy's torpedo floatplane, replacing the Laté 29; its twin floats held fuel, and a torpedo, bombs or depth charges hung between them. In service from 1938, it struck German armoured columns in 1940 with relatively light losses and last saw combat in 1944, attacking Channel shipping. In the game it turns very well but is slower than nearly every biplane; a high 450 km/h structural limit allows boom-and-zoom, while two 7.5 mm guns with 500 rounds each are weak. It can also capture points in naval battles. It was a 2022 Winter Quest reward in "Apex Predators".
leo_451_early: The LeO 451 was a French light bomber programme of the early 1930s; a first prototype with Hispano-Suiza engines took off in 1937 and production ramped up quickly before May 1940, when it suffered heavily under German air superiority but fared better against Italy. In the game it is a fast, versatile medium bomber able to hit tanks, pillboxes and similar point targets from low level, and its 1,900 kg maximum load is respectable next to the Pe-2 or Cant Z.1007bis and enough for bases. It is also agile for a twin-engined bomber. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
leo_451_late: The late LeO 451 reflects revisions made to improve the bomber's survivability, the most important of which, in service before France's surrender, gave the rear gunner light machine guns alongside his Hispano 404 cannon. Developed from the early 1930s and first flown in 1937, the type suffered heavy losses to the Luftwaffe in 1940 but did better against Italy. In the game it shares the early model's speed, agility and versatile 1,900 kg load for low-level strikes or base bombing, while two extra 7.5 mm guns strengthen its rear defence.
lightning_f53: By the late 1960s the Lightning was being superseded in RAF service, so new-build F.53s, ground-attack versions of the F.6 with extra hardpoints for bombs and rocket pods, were exported to Kuwait (12 F.53Ks) and Saudi Arabia (34); the Saudis used them heavily from 1967 to 1986, replacing them with Tornado IDS from 1989. In the game the extra weight makes its already mediocre dogfighting a little worse, but it excels at fast frontline strike runs with up to 192 unguided rockets in underwing and overwing pods and an internal bay. A premium pack from the "Danger Zone" update, it left the store after the 2022 Winter sale.
lightning_f6: English Electric's Lightning, conceived in the late 1940s after the Miles M.52 was cancelled, was a high-performance interceptor against Soviet bombers with distinctive stacked engines. The F.6, the last production model, joined the RAF in December 1965 with a bigger ventral tank, a new wing and 30 mm ADEN cannons restored; Lightnings were the RAF's main interceptor for much of the 1960s and 1970s. In the game it offers decent acceleration, climb and top speed and carries two Firestreak or Red Top missiles, capable weapons, though having only two means picking shots carefully. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
lincoln_b2: Avro's Lincoln began in 1944 as an improved Lancaster to Specification B.14/43, with the Mk II prototype originally called the Lancaster Mk V; it first flew on 9 June 1944, but the B-29 had already overtaken it. After the war Lincolns fought insurgents in Kenya and Malaya until V-bombers replaced them, and 604 were built. In the game it keeps the Lancaster's strengths with better handling and much stronger defence, two Hispano cannons and four Brownings. It accelerates well enough to climb high or dive in fast, but the airframe is still fragile, so interceptors are best avoided or engaged at long range. It came in Update 1.67 "Assault".
loire_130: Chosen in a 1936 French Navy contest for a ship-based scout, the Loire 130 entered production in 1937 as the standard M and the colonial C, which had a bigger radiator and a Hispano-Suiza 12Ycrs engine; 125 were built, nearly every French warship carried one by the late 1930s, and they served until 1951. In the game it flies averagely but, unlike many catapult aircraft, carries guns: two turrets with 7.5 mm machine guns covering front and rear, plus two 75 kg bombs that can sink an unwary coastal boat. Against most opponents it meets, it is slow and easy to hit. It came in Update 2.27 "La Royale".
lynx_ah_mk1: Westland developed the Lynx from the mid-1960s to succeed its Scout and Wasp; the prototype flew in March 1971, later set helicopter speed records, and the Army ordered 100. Lynxes have since served from the Falklands and the Gulf to the Balkans and Somalia, with about 450 built by 2009. In the game it is a big step up from the Wasp: quicker and nimbler, with Hydra-70 rockets, AGM-114B Hellfires or a 20 mm cannon, always two AIM-92 Stingers, thermal sights and ample countermeasures. It has no armour, though, and weak gunner zoom makes distant targets hard to spot. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
m_346fa: The M-346 began as a joint trainer project with Yakovlev in the early 1990s; when the partnership ended in 2000, Yakovlev went on to the Yak-130 while Aermacchi reworked the design with Western avionics, new materials and Honeywell F124 engines, flying it in July 2004. The armed M-346FA, unveiled in 2017 with a GRIFO 346 radar, radar and missile warning, countermeasures and weapon pylons, first flew in pre-production form in 2020. In the game it is responsive and agile like the Yak-130, but slow and very exposed to attack, so its many stores suit pure ground attack. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
martin_139wc: China bought nine export Martin 139W bombers, a version of the B-10, in 1936 with funds raised for Chiang Kai-shek's 50th birthday; they achieved little early in the war with Japan, but on 20 May 1938 they dropped propaganda leaflets over Kyushu, four years before the Doolittle Raid. Obsolete once Soviet and American bombers arrived, they ended up as training aids until 1945. In the game its boat-like shape and weak defensive guns hold it back, but up to 600 kg of bombs is a solid load at its rank for destroying stationary targets. It came with the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
marut_mk1: India's HF-24 Marut, named after the storm gods, was HAL's attempt at a supersonic fighter-bomber, designed with the help of Kurt Tank of Fw 190 fame. The prototype flew in June 1961 on Orpheus 703 power that proved too weak for supersonic flight, and with no better engine obtainable, all 147 were built that way; they saw action only in the 1971 war with Pakistan and were retired by 1982. In the game it has good guns and a strong selection of ground-attack weapons, but it is subsonic, handles poorly and carries no air-to-air missiles. It was a 2025 "Spirit of the Tempest" event reward in the British tree.
maryland_mk1_france: Glenn L. Martin's Model 167 lost a 1937 US Army attack-aircraft contest to the Douglas DB-7, but France ordered 200, fitted with French equipment. An American embargo delayed deliveries until early 1940, yet in some 400 sorties during the Battle of France only 4% were lost, against 16% for the LeO 451. Evacuated to North Africa after the armistice, they fought the British under Vichy, notably in Syria and Lebanon, until B-26s replaced them in 1943. In the game it is fast, agile and climbs well, but its defensive guns are weak, its bomb load modest and it has no armour. It came in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
mb_151c1: After losing the 1934 fighter contest to the MS.406, Marcel Bloch reworked his M.B.150 for easier production as the M.B.151, with a 920 hp engine, smaller wing, simpler undercarriage and four 7.5 mm machine guns in place of a cannon. Despite overheating and disappointing handling, 140 were built from January 1939 out of necessity, and they could match neither the Bf 110's speed nor the Bf 109E's agility. In the game it is nimble for a monoplane, climbs decently and dives fast, but any biplane will out-turn it, its guns are weak and it has no ordnance. It was a 2024 Winter Tales prize in the "Storm Warning" update.
mb_152c1: A modern design with retractable undercarriage, Bloch's M.B.152 was developed from 1934 as a successor to the D.371; 482 were built between 1938 and 1942, serving France and then Vichy, with some flown by the Luftwaffe. In the game it is versatile, combining good agility, a respectable top speed and a decent climb, though many monoplane fighters are faster. Its Hispano 404 cannons have little ammunition and the rifle-calibre machine guns do little damage, so shots must count. It was a reward in the 2018 Festive Quest.
mb_157: The final step in Bloch's M.B.150 family, which had grown into the 920 hp M.B.151 and 1,050 hp M.B.152, the M.B.157 paired the design with a 1,590 hp engine; just a single prototype was completed, and it never saw service. In the game it is a solid boom-and-zoom fighter: climb is average, so side-climbing early helps, but the strong engine gives good level speed for diving on unaware targets, and it is nimble enough to dogfight well in capable hands. Ammunition is limited, so bursts need to be measured. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
mb_162: Derived from Bloch's M.B.160 airliner but sharing little with it, the M.B.162 heavy bomber had a different wing layout and a cargo bay reworked to hold bombs; Germany captured it before it could enter service. Bloch's company later became Dassault Aviation. In the game it is the strongest of the French tree's home-grown bombers and plays rather like a B-17, quick at altitude with a load large enough for a base or several ground targets. Its 20 mm cannons cover only a narrow arc and the nose has no guns at all, leaving it exposed to frontal attacks. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
mb_174_a3: Designed at the former Bloch works, by then nationalised under SNCASO, to a 1936 requirement for a light bomber and reconnaissance aircraft, the twin-engined M.B.170 first flew in February 1938 and evolved into the three-seat M.B.174A.3, in service from March 1940. Fast and agile enough to evade German interceptors, it was well liked, but after France fell it was relegated to auxiliary tasks under Vichy, such as watching the British fleet at Gibraltar; production stopped at 56. In the game it flies very well for a bomber, but its modest bomb load struggles to destroy bases or ground vehicles reliably. It was introduced in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
mb_175t: A post-war naval conversion of the Bloch MB.170, the M.B.175T came about while France was rearming with whatever it had; a single F5W torpedo and long range made it a maritime patrol aircraft until more modern types like the F6F replaced it in 1950. In the game it is more attacker than bomber: two 20 mm MG 151/20 cannons and HVAR rockets make it a handy bomber interceptor, particularly against the BV 238. In naval battles one well-aimed torpedo can sink a ship, but its large size makes it an easy target for anti-aircraft fire. It arrived in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
mb_326b: Aermacchi's MB-326, first flown on 10 December 1957, was a light all-metal jet trainer that could also fight, and at least 800 were built, with Brazil the largest user. The MB-326B was its first attack version, ordered by Tunisia in 1965 with six underwing pylons. In the game it carries a varied load of bombs, rockets, napalm or up to six miniguns, but has no built-in guns and a much weaker engine than the MB-326K. It handles well for a jet, yet rarely reaches top speed outside a long dive, especially when loaded, and lags behind most WWII jets. It came in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
mb_326k: Developed for South Africa from 1966, the MB-326K turned the MB-326 trainer into a dedicated attacker, swapping 7.62 mm guns for two 30 mm DEFA 553 cannons and adding provision for more pods and bombs; at least 93 were built, 73 of them licence-built Impala Mk IIs. In the game it is a specialised ground attacker with bombs, rockets and napalm, and its built-in 30 mm cannons, plus optional cannon pods or as many as six miniguns, make it dangerous to aircraft too. It flies well when clean, but a heavy load leaves it slower and clumsier than most WWII jets. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
mb_5: A premium British fighter, the MB.5 looks and flies much like a P-51D, but with a Spitfire-style nose, a contra-rotating propeller like the Wyvern's and four 20 mm Hispano Mk II cannons in place of the Mustang's six .50 cals. Its speed, punch and strong climb make it an effective interceptor or air-superiority fighter against German and Soviet peers. Turn rate is below average overall, though at high speed it can turn surprisingly sharply, and its power limits energy loss in vertical manoeuvres. Sold as a pack from Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm", it left the store after the 2019 Victory Day Sale.
mbr-2: Beriev's MBR-2 was a 1930s multi-purpose flying boat for Soviet naval patrol, and this version takes its name from its AM-34NB engine, which improved performance and reliability; with a range over 1,000 km, it also served as a light bomber and submarine hunter during WWII. In the game it is at its best in ground battles, offering many close-support loadouts and surprising agility for its size to dodge fighters and place bombs accurately. Its defensive guns are adequate, but with no armour, vital parts are easily hit. It was a reward in the 2016 "Chronicles of World War II" event in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
mc-202: This Macchi C. 202 Folgore in the German tree has been in the game since the open beta; when the Italian tree arrived in Update 1.69 it moved there, but players who unlocked it earlier keep it. Without bombs or rockets it is purely a fighter, combining good speed, a very good climb and fast roll with a sturdy airframe. It turns best at high speed, while slow flat turns are a mistake unless the roll rate is used to gain position. Its 12.7 mm and 7.7 mm guns need long bursts, lose punch beyond about 300 m and struggle against bombers.
mc-202_d: The C. 202D Folgore was handed out as a reward in the 2021 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. event during the "Winged Lions" update. With no bombs or rockets, it is a pure fighter, pairing good speed with strong climb and roll rates and a sturdy airframe that can bring it home after a few hits. It turns well at high speed, but slow flat turns are best avoided unless its roll rate can create an advantage. The guns are adequate, though many opponents are better armed.
mc-202_ec: The C. 202EC ("Esperimento Cannoni") added 20 mm MG 151/20 cannons under the wings once intensifying Allied bombing in early 1943 showed that the Folgore's guns, chosen with fighters in mind, were too weak for B-17s, B-24s and similar bombers. About 50 were built new and around 100 converted in the field. In the game the two cannons let it bring down both bombers and fighters with ease, while it keeps the C. 202's agility, climb and speed. Its many fuel tanks make it fragile, though, often catching fire or exploding when hit, so it rewards skilled pilots. It came in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
mc-202_italy: Mario Castoldi's C.202 Folgore succeeded the C.200 and proved highly effective after entering service in 1941, mostly in North Africa until 1943, then over Sicily and in small numbers against the Soviet Union; 1,150 were built before the C.205 took over. In the game, where an identical version previously sat in the German tree, it is a pure air-superiority fighter with good speed, an excellent climb and quick roll. Lacking cannons, its 12.7 mm and 7.7 mm guns manage against fighters only with long bursts and are poor against bombers, so it wins through performance rather than firepower. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
mc-205_n2: The C.205N "Orione" was a redesign of the C.205V with bigger wings and a longer fuselage; the first prototype, armed only with 12.7 mm guns, was rejected, but the 1943 N2 added a stronger engine and an engine-mounted 20 mm cannon and was accepted, only to be abandoned amid shortages and the armistice. In the game it is excellent at both turning and energy fights, agile at high and low speed alike, and its three 20 mm cannons plus two 12.7 mm guns, especially with incendiary-rich air belts, need only a few hits. It came with the first Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
mc-205_serie1: Once Germany allowed DB 605A production in Italy, Macchi developed the C.205 Veltro; it first flew on 19 April 1942 and entered service in February 1943, mainly defending Italian airspace, and served both sides after the armistice. The 1st series of 100 aircraft carried two 12.7 mm and two 7.7 mm guns. In the game it balances agility and speed well, comfortable in turning or energy fights and able to tighten turns with combat flaps. The weak guns need many hits, and survivability is poor against the cannon-armed opponents it meets. It came with the first Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
mc-205_serie3: A refined C. 205 serie 1, the serie 3 fixes the type's biggest weakness by adding a 20 mm MG 151/20 cannon in each wing to the two cowling-mounted 12.7 mm guns. The extra weight takes a little off the DB 605-powered fighter's performance and it meets tougher opponents, but it stays versatile, happy to boom-and-zoom, energy fight or turn as needed, and the twin cannons shred whatever they hit. It joined the game with the first Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
mc200_serie3: Mario Castoldi's C.200 Saetta was Macchi's first fully in-house design to reach mass production, entering service in 1938 and fighting from September 1940 across southern Europe, North Africa and the Eastern Front; it held its own until newer Allied fighters appeared in 1942. The 3rd series introduced a fixed tailwheel, and over 1,100 Saettas were built by Macchi, Breda and SAI-Ambrosini. In this German-tree version, present since the open beta, it excels in turning fights, beating almost anything but biplanes, while boom-and-zoom works only once before energy runs out. Climb is low and low-level speed average, and the twin heavy machine guns suit fighters better than bombers.
mc200_serie3_italy: The Italian tree's C. 200 serie 3 arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", though a version had already existed in the German tree. A typical pre-war Italian fighter, it has moderate speed, good turning, high speed tolerance with good control throughout, a respectable climb and a sturdy airframe, but its weak engine hampers acceleration. Its two 12.7 mm Breda-SAFAT guns are modest, best fired within 300 m with tracer, air or stealth belts, and too weak for bombers other than early biplanes such as the Swordfish. With no bombs modelled, it can only harm soft ground targets.
mc200_serie7: A later Saetta from Mario Castoldi's team at Macchi, the C.200 serie 7 brought only minor changes over the serie 3: revised radio gear and extra fuel tanks. In the German tree since before the open beta, it plays almost identically to its predecessor, with good handling and agility and well-regarded fixed guns. The extra tanks make it easier to damage, however, and the engine becomes temperamental once hit.
mc200_serie7_italy: Added to the Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", this C. 200 serie 7 also had an earlier counterpart in the German tree. It shows the classic pre-war Italian formula: middling speed, strong turning and good control even when fast, a climb that matches many rivals and enough toughness to limp home after hits. Its shortcomings are a weak engine that limits acceleration and a modest armament of two 12.7 mm Breda-SAFATs firing through the propeller. Without modelled bombs, it can only threaten soft ground targets.
md_450b_barougan: The Barougan (Arabic for "battle") was a small offshoot of Dassault's Ouragan, fitted with a four-wheel main undercarriage to cope with grass strips and a tail parachute to shorten landings; it worked, but budget cuts ended the programme and the aircraft reverted to standard. In the game it is a decent early jet with four 20 mm chin cannons, bombs and SNEB rockets, though poor belts limit the guns. Its Rolls-Royce engine is adequate, but heavy fuel loads ruin acceleration and energy retention. It is a useful stepping stone in the French tree towards later home-grown jets. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
md_450b_ouragan: Dassault's Ouragan, in service from 1952, was France's first home-built jet aircraft and served for decades as a fighter-bomber, with export users including Israel and India. The M.D.450B, the second production version, had an uprated Nene 104B and revised undercarriage doors, since gunfire tended to damage the originals. In the game it is a strong air-superiority jet for its rank: acceleration is slow even by jet standards, but it reaches a good top speed and holds energy well under 700 km/h, though it compresses heavily above 850 km/h. Its 1,000 lb bombs and rockets can deal with a few tanks. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
md_450b_ouragan_iaf: After failed attempts to buy F-86s and F-84s, and with its intended Mystères grounded by problems, Israel received 12 Ouragans from France as a stopgap; even after the Mystère IV arrived it kept flying them as support fighters and strike aircraft into the 1970s, selling some to El Salvador. In the game it is average but versatile: a 942 km/h top speed makes chasing or escaping hard, and the 1,030 km/h structural limit calls for care in dives. It turns well and keeps energy in manoeuvres, and can carry rockets and assorted bombs. It came in the "Winged Lions" update.
md_450b_ouragan_iaf_29: Israel's first Ouragans reached Hazor on 6 October 1955 for the new 113th Squadron, and the fleet grew to 75, flying mostly ground attack in conflicts including Suez and the Six-Day War while also scoring air victories, among them MiG-21s. Aircraft "29", flown by Captain Jaacon Agasi, joined the 31 October 1956 attack on the Egyptian destroyer Mohammed Ali el-Kebir, which then surrendered. In the game it resembles early jets like the F-80 and Meteor: agile with concentrated nose guns but slow to accelerate and modest in top speed, with a small payload for light attack. Its camouflage sets it apart. It came in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
md_452_mystere_2a: Dassault's Mystère II took the M.D.450 as its starting point, adding more power and a swept wing for higher speed and better agility when fast; the IIA designation covered the second and third pre-production prototypes, which, unlike later versions, used a Rolls-Royce Tay. In the game it resembles the earlier M.D.450 but depends more on high-speed performance, sitting mid-pack for speed among its peers. Like a delta-wing jet it bleeds energy quickly in hard manoeuvres, so it should stay fast, pick off distracted enemies and act as a support fighter. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
md_452_mystere_2c_preproduction: First of the production Mystère IIs, the IIC had a new engine that could take it past the speed of sound in certain conditions; France ordered 14 pre-series examples in 1951 and eventually 150, but the more advanced Mystère IVA was almost ready by the time the IIC reached units, and the last ones served as combat trainers. In the game it flies almost exactly like its predecessor; a relatively weak engine makes holding energy difficult, so hit-and-run attacks suit it best, and a good roll rate helps shake pursuers when a dogfight cannot be avoided. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
md_454_mystere_4a: France's Mystère IVA plays much like the delta-wing jets in the game: good top speed, a capable engine, sharp high-speed handling and excellent angle of attack for dogfights, but hard manoeuvres scrub off speed rapidly. Its two 30 mm DEFA cannons have easy ballistics and hit hard, though they fire more slowly than the 20 mm cannons or .50 cal Brownings on many American fighters. Long fights are best avoided: it should use its agility at speed to snap a quick shot, then fly straight to rebuild energy. It was added in the "Red Skies" update.
md_454_mystere_4a_iaf: Israel ordered 24 Mystère IVAs in 1955, receiving them in two batches in April 1956, and another 36 arrived through Operation 'Shaharit', for 61 in total. In the Suez Crisis they flew 147 sorties for the loss of one aircraft while claiming Egyptian MiG-15s and Vampires. In the game it is a strong dogfighter when it has energy, and its two 30 mm DEFA cannons destroy aircraft in a few hits. Below about 700 km/h it bleeds speed badly, so keeping above roughly 850 km/h preserves its fighting ability and helps dodge missiles; weak acceleration favours a patient style. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
md_460: Dassault's Super Mystère B2 crowned the line that ran from the Ouragan through the Mystère II, III and IV, and was France's first aircraft to go supersonic in level flight; the multi-role fighter-bomber sold to Israel, El Salvador and Honduras. In the game its afterburner makes it a capable interceptor, with two 30 mm DEFA 552 cannons plus SNEB or T10 151 rockets and AA-20 Nord or AIM-9B missiles; the guns can finish off targets left slowed by a missile. Set up for ground attack it gives up speed and agility but carries up to 2,000 lb of bombs. It came in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
md_460_saar: The Sa'ar was Israel's answer to the Super Mystère's weak, thirsty and unreliable Atar 101G-3: from 1967 it received the A-4H's J52-P-8A, more powerful and economical but without an afterburner, plus extra ground-attack capability, Shafrir 2 missiles and longer range, and all 26 Israeli aircraft were converted by 1973. In the game it inherits some Skyhawk weaknesses; top speed is fine for a subsonic jet, but acceleration and energy retention are poor, and bombs make it easy prey for MiG-19s and MiG-21s. It works best as a support fighter, since its AIM-9D-like Shafrir 2 meets few countermeasures. It came in "Winged Lions".
md_460_sambad: Israel ordered 24 Super Mystère B2s, called Sambad, in 1958 after the Suez Crisis exposed its need for a jet with more range and endurance; its first supersonic fighter, it saw heavy use in the Six-Day War, including the USS Liberty incident, and again in 1973. In the game it handles like a delta: violent manoeuvres are possible with speed, but low-speed handling is awful, energy retention poor and acceleration mediocre low down. It suits support work, using the afterburner to climb or stay fast on the edges of a fight and picking off slow or damaged targets with guns or Shafrir missiles. It came in "Winged Lions".
md_460_yt_cup_2019: This Super Mystère B2 was the grand prize of the 2019 YouTube Cup, added in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy". The type was Dassault's final evolution of the Ouragan and Mystère line and the first French aircraft to exceed Mach 1 in level flight, which helped it sell abroad. It plays as a true multi-role jet: with afterburner it can intercept fighters or bombers using two DEFA 552 cannons, rockets and Nord or Sidewinder missiles, while bomb loads of 1,000 or 2,000 lb can hit ships, hardened targets and bases at some cost to speed and agility.
md_500_tow_late: Israel bought the MD 500 after the Yom Kippur War as a cheap addition to its Cobra fleet, taking 32 after 1977 trials and six more in 1984; carrying four TOWs or rocket pods and an electro-optical sight in a turret, it fought in southern Lebanon and against Syrian armour on the Beirut–Damascus highway. In the game the Lahatut is small and nimble, much harder to spot or hit than larger helicopters such as the Mi-24D. It carries 14 Hydra 70 rockets or four BGM-71D TOW-2s, among the fastest helicopter ATGMs at its rank and ideal for ambushes near the front. It came in "Danger Zone".
me-163b: The Me 163 B Komet, a German rocket fighter, has been in the game since the open beta. Few jets can outrun, out-climb or out-turn it, and its airframe is sturdy enough to take extreme manoeuvres, but its fuel lasts only about six minutes, which is its main weakness. The usual approach is to rocket up high early, cut the engine and glide in at speed, staying above 5,000 m and using vertical manoeuvres to keep energy while preying on enemies still climbing. Its huge thrust gets it into the fight early, but chasing top jets wastes fuel, so letting them come is wiser.
me-163b-0: Developed around Helmut Walter's rocket engine to counter Allied bomber raids, the Me 163 first flew in 1941, but toxic fuel and fuel-line problems caused poisonings and explosions; about 450 were built and only one of three units became combat-ready, claiming roughly nine to 16 kills for some 11 losses. The B-0 was the first production series, 47 of which carried MG 151/20 cannons. In the game its fuselage and underwing 20 mm cannons give it more firepower than later Komets, along with excellent acceleration and climb, but its top speed falls short against likely opponents, so surprise attacks are essential. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
me-262a-1a: Messerschmitt's Me 262 Schwalbe was the first jet fighter to enter operational service, and the A-1a carried four 30 mm cannons plus air-to-air rockets. In service from mid-1944, it fought the first jet air combat on 26 July 1944 against a Mosquito and was credited with 542 Allied aircraft, but unreliable engines, shortages and Hitler's bomber ambitions blunted it. In the game it plays as a genuine heavy fighter: rockets break up bomber formations and the MK 108s shred B-17s in seconds, though their low velocity takes practice, and faster, nimbler jets can outmatch it. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-262a-1a_early: Messerschmitt's Project 1065 evolved from a straight-winged design into the swept-wing Me 262, which flew first with a piston engine in April 1941 and on Jumo 004A jets in June 1942; engine shortages delayed production until summer 1944. In units the A-1a came as a fighter or as the Jabo fighter-bomber, which differed only in carrying bombs and anti-tank rockets and was later reworked into the A-2 Sturmvogel. In the game it is manoeuvrable, heavily armed and, unlike the standard A-1a, carries a good bomb load, but it shares early jets' poor acceleration, slow climb and rapid energy loss in turns. It arrived in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
me-262a-1a_u4: The Pulkzerstörer, or "Narwal", was a 1943 concept for an Me 262 bomber destroyer with one 50 mm Mk 214 gun developed from the Pak 38; its two prototypes carried a BK 5 until the refined Mk 214a was ready, testing ran in March–April 1945, and it never entered production. In the game that single cannon replaces the usual four MK 108s; slow fire and poor accuracy, especially when stock, make small targets hard to hit, but one hit destroys anything short of a heavy bomber. Its speed lets it pounce on piston fighters, and HVAP-T shells make it an effective tank-buster. It came in Update 1.41.
me-262a-2a: The A-2 Sturmvogel came from reworking the Me 262 Jabo fighter-bomber with full bomb racks and two of its four MK 108 cannons removed; like other Me 262s it was mostly used against bombers, with relatively few serving as ground attackers, and Czechoslovakia flew the type until 1951. In the game it is fairly fast and nimble, with strong guns and a useful bomb load, but suffers the usual early-jet faults of sluggish acceleration, weak climb and quick energy loss in manoeuvres. It was a reward in the 2016 Winter Holiday event.
me-262a1_u1: One of several experimental Me 262 versions, the A-1a/U1 swapped the standard four MK 108s for a mixed battery of two 20 mm MG 151/20s, two 30 mm MK 103s and two 30 mm MK 108s for more punch and dependability; no more than three were built. In the game the revised guns and high speed make it a more flexible Me 262, able to hit both aircraft and ground targets. It is fragile, though, and handles poorly below about 350 km/h or above 700 km/h, leaving a narrow band where it flies well. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
me-262c-1a: The Heimatschützer ("home protector") was a single Me 262A fitted with the Me 163's Walter HWK 109-509 rocket engine in the tail to speed interceptions; it first flew on combined jet and rocket power on 27 February 1945. In the game the booster gives a very fast climb, but its fuel lasts only a few minutes. Once it runs dry, the aircraft is essentially an Me 262 A-1a with the same guns, engines and airframe, made slightly worse by the extra weight. It was introduced in Update 1.39.
me-262c-2b: Conceived in 1943 as a high-performance bomber interceptor, the Me 262 C-2b kept the A-series jets and added a rocket booster atop each engine exhaust; the sole prototype flew in March 1945, climbing to 9,100 m in three minutes, far too late to matter. In the game it has the A-series' four nose MK 108s, whose low velocity and short effective range struggle at jet ranks.
