About six minutes of booster fuel is best spent reaching a useful speed, since once it is gone many opponents outclass it, making it a capable but demanding aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.41.
me-410a-1: The Me 410 grew from the Me 210, looking similar but with far stronger DB 603 engines, and the A-1 was meant as a fast bomber, a role it handled poorly, as two 500 kg bombs only just fitted. In the game it is the earliest Me 410 in the tree with bombs, either two 500 kg, two 250 kg or eight 50 kg, a light load for bases. Two MG 151s and two 7.92 mm guns help against soft targets, and 13 mm side turrets give some defence, but fighters remain a threat. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410a-1_u2: When Bomber Command lost faith in the Me 410 as a fast bomber and the Luftwaffe needed heavy fighters, the A-1/U2 led the shift, dropping bombs for the WB 151A pack that added two more MG 151s, for four cannons and two 7.92 mm guns in total; production moved to this standard and existing A-1s were converted. In the game, close to the B-1/U2, its guns down fighters and bombers easily, but sluggish performance makes climbing to bombers hard and enemy fighters are far superior. It works best alongside teammates, picking off distracted or badly placed targets. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410a-1_u4: Once the Me 410 was refocused from bombing to bomber-destroying, a 1943 order for heavy cannon armament led to the 50 mm BK 5, adapted from a tank gun; around 60 A-1/U4s were built before the gun was judged excessive and later versions simply took extra smaller cannons. In the game the BK 5 carries a generous 22 rounds, with optional APCBC-HE-T, HVAP-T or Minengeschoß belts, while the default belt mixes AP-T and HEI-T, which suits neither role well. Loading armour-piercing rounds in the big gun and using the MG 151s against aircraft is the most effective setup. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410b-1: The Me 410 B was meant to get DB 603G engines, but they never arrived, so it was essentially an A with more fuel, a stronger undercarriage and oxygen for high altitude. The B-1 came from the period when the type was still a fast bomber, so it keeps a bomb bay and lacks the extra cannon packs of later models. In the game its maximum of two 500 kg bombs is weak even for a light bomber, though 13 mm guns in place of the A-1's 7.92 mm add a little firepower, still far short of the B-6/R3. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410b-1_u2: Essentially the A-1/U2 with the B-series changes of extra fuel, sturdier undercarriage and an oxygen system, the B-1/U2 was built to break up bomber formations, with the WB 151A pack adding two MG 151s, plus an armoured windscreen and fighter gunsight. In the game it resembles other Me 410s but carries more guns and Wfr.Gr.21 rockets. The only real difference from the A-1/U2 is that two 13 mm machine guns replace the 7.92 mm pair; otherwise they perform the same. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410b-2_u4: Because DB 603G engines were scarce, early Me 410 Bs kept the A's DB 603A, though some gained oxygen gear and a better undercarriage. The B-2/U4 added a 5 cm cannon under the nose and two 20 mm MG 151s from the Waffenbehälter kit; about 130 were made, by Messerschmitt and Dornier. In the game it attacks ground targets well, the BK 5 offering HVAP or AP rounds, the latter devastating when fired down into tank roofs, with MG 151 support. Twin 13 mm side turrets defend it, but it has no bombs or rockets. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me-410b-6_r3: The Me 410 B-6 was a naval Zerstörer for escorting German ships and U-boats, with a FuG 200 radio for talking to submarines and two 30 mm MK 103s beside its MG 151s; only a handful were built, and after France was lost they were reduced to rescue work. In the game its nose cannons are lethal, and armour-piercing MK 103 rounds can penetrate many tanks' engine decks. Armour and engines are unchanged from other Me 410s, so it remains sluggish and exposed to fighters, while its two 13 mm turrets have narrow arcs. It has been in the game since the open beta.
me_210_v22_japan: Meant to replace the Bf 110, the Me 210 flew in September 1939 but proved unstable, stall-prone and underpowered, and the Me 410 soon superseded it. Prototype V22 (GE+KV), lengthened during 1942 trials at Rechlin to improve handling, reached Japan by submarine in January 1943; Kawasaki assembled it, the Army was unimpressed, and after damage to its landing gear and engine mounts Kawasaki used it for its own tests. In the game it improves little on the German Me 210: slow, poor in the climb and clumsy, but with decent forward and defensive guns and a bomb bay. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
me_210a_1: Messerschmitt's answer to a request for a Bf 110 successor, the Me 210 added a redesigned nose, an internal bomb bay, an unusual defensive gun system and a more swept wing, and 1,000 were ordered before its first flight in September 1939. It proved unstable and stall-prone, yet the A-1 was rushed to units in April 1942, with production halted at 90, and it served briefly in Africa and Italy before the Me 410 took over. In the game it is slow, climbs poorly and handles badly, though its forward and defensive armament is decent and it has a bomb bay. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
me_210ca_1_40_mm_hungary: Hungary's Me 210 Ca-1 cured the original's stability and stall problems with a longer fuselage and gained much stronger DB 605B engines. A few carried a 40 mm cannon derived from the Bofors gun for use against bombers, plus licence-built 15 cm rockets for ground targets; Hungarian Me 210s served from 1943 until crews destroyed them in March 1945. In the game this is the most capable strike version of the Me 210: its 40 mm gun, 50 kg bombs and Wgr. 41 Spr. rockets handle armour, and the engines allow fast attack runs. Rear 13 mm MG 131s offer only modest defence. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
me_210ca_1_hungary: Built by Dunai Repülőgépgyár from 1943 until Allied bombing in 1944, the Me 210 Ca-1 used a longer fuselage and DB 605B engines to cure the German original's poor handling, and Hungary flew it successfully as a light attacker rather than the intended heavy fighter until crews destroyed the survivors in March 1945. In the game it is a strong strike fighter: two 20 mm MG 151s and two MG 17s deal with aircraft and light vehicles, and bombs of up to 1,000 kg handle tougher targets. Powerful engines help it through flak, but it is no dogfighter. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
me_264: Messerschmitt's Me 264 was its entry for the "Amerika Bomber" requirement, a four-engined heavy bomber with roughly 11,000 km of range; it was outclassed by Junkers' six-engined Ju 390, Dönitz talked Hitler out of a U-boat reconnaissance version, and Göring halted work after bombing damaged the prototypes. In the game it is a formidable heavy bomber carrying up to 4,350 kg (two 1,800 kg and three 250 kg bombs), defended by two 13 mm and three 20 mm turrets, and with a 519 km/h top speed and a very high air spawn it is hard to stop. It came in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
meteor_fmk3: Gloster's Meteor was the only Allied jet to fight in WWII; development began in 1940, it entered service in July 1944 and was downing V-1 flying bombs from 4 August, and the Derwent I-powered F Mk 3 followed in December 1944, later defending Belgium and the Netherlands. In the game it is a balanced all-rounder and a good first jet: slower than the Attacker and less agile than the Vampire, but still nimble enough to draw opponents into turning fights, where its four nose Hispanos finish them quickly. Weak engines and a stiff roll rate are its main flaws. It has been in the game since the open beta.
meteor_fmk3_navy: Two Meteor F Mk 3s were converted for naval use in 1948 and tested aboard HMS Illustrious and Implacable, gaining tail hooks, strengthened bellies and undercarriage, and more powerful Derwent 5 engines; the Navy liked them but chose the Supermarine Attacker instead. In the game those engines, nearly twice as strong as the F Mk 3's, cure its lack of thrust but make it frighteningly easy to overspeed, even shedding its wings in level flight, so the airbrake is essential in dives and hard manoeuvres. Kept under control, it turns as well as other Meteors and has thrust to spare. It has been in the game since the open beta.
meteor_fmk4_lw: The Meteor F Mk 4 improved on the F Mk 3 with Derwent 5 engines, more fuel and a stronger airframe; it first flew on 15 August 1945 and 535 were built by March 1949 for the RAF and export customers. This early G.41F version kept the longer wing, which favoured climb and high-altitude performance over agility at low and medium heights. In the game it pairs strong guns with respectable handling, so it is dangerous in the air, but it carries no ordnance, so it cannot help ground forces. It was introduced in Update 1.29.
meteor_fmk4_sw: Clipping the wing of the Meteor F Mk 4 produced the G.41G, which turned and handled better at low and medium altitude at the expense of high-altitude performance, and it became the most common F Mk 4 in frontline RAF service. The F Mk 4 itself brought Derwent 5 engines, more fuel and a stronger airframe, with 535 built from 1945 to 1949. In the game it combines effective guns with balanced handling and is a tough opponent in air battles, but its limited external stores leave it as a pure fighter. It arrived in Update 1.29.
meteor_fmk8_belgium: Belgium built up a fleet of some 240 Meteor F Mk.8s, starting with about thirty from Gloster in 1949, then a larger batch from Fokker in the Netherlands and around seventy assembled locally by Avions Fairey at Gosselies; they formed much of the country's jet fighter force until 1963. This one wears the colours of 'EG224', which is preserved at the Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History in Brussels. It sits in the French tree and arrived in the "Seek & Destroy" update.
meteor_fmk8_iaf: Britain's Meteor F Mk.8 reached Israel during the regional arms race of the 1950s, with 11 delivered in 1953–54; they flew with several squadrons, saw action in the Suez Crisis and left frontline service in 1956, continuing as trainers. In the game it is a support and frontline fighter with strong acceleration and good low-speed agility. Staying aware of the battle and choosing winnable fights is what keeps it alive. It arrived with the first Israeli air tree in the "Winged Lions" update.
meteor_fmk8_reaper: The Reaper was a dedicated ground-attack development of the Meteor F Mk.8 (G.41K) that never progressed past the prototype; its modifications would have let it carry twice the standard F.8's payload. Korea showed that the Meteor had reached its limits, and with the Hunter, Swift and foreign equivalents arriving, interest faded. In the game it is a British premium, first sold as a pack in Update 1.85 "Supersonic", withdrawn after War Thunder's 7th anniversary and later offered for Golden Eagles after the 8th.
meteor_frmk9_iaf: The FR.9 was the reconnaissance version of the Meteor F Mk.8, with a nose 22 cm longer holding a remotely operated F.24 camera; 126 were built in 1952, and pilots found it kept the fighter's agility apart from slightly worse high-speed stability and control. Israel received seven ex-RAF examples in 1955, one of which shot down two Egyptian Vampires that year, and flew them on reconnaissance until 1962. In the game it is almost an F.8 with marginally weaker flight performance: nimble, lively and well stocked with ammunition, but slow to roll and quick to lose energy in long turns. It was a 2025 "Eye in the Sky" event reward.
meteor_nfmk13: Britain offered Meteor NF.13 night fighters around the Middle East to win sales while staying neutral, and Israel, needing night-fighting capability, took up an offer originally made to Syria and Egypt, ordering six in 1956 for the new 119th Squadron; three arrived that year and three in 1958. In the game its radar can find aircraft at medium and high altitude, useful against unseen bombers, and strong engines give quick acceleration, good energy retention and a fast cruise. It rolls slowly, its wing guns are awkward at short range, and with no ordnance it is purely an air-to-air aircraft. It came in "Winged Lions".
mh_60l_dap: Sikorsky's S-70 won the US Army's contest for a UH-1 replacement and entered service in 1979 as the UH-60 Black Hawk; the armed MH-60L followed in 1987, and some were reworked for special forces as the DAP (Direct Action Penetrator), with rockets, Hellfires and air-to-air missiles, a cabin for door gunners only and an extra fuel tank. In the game it looks like a utility helicopter but carries stub wings with four pylons and an arsenal close to the AH-64D's: AGM-114K Hellfire IIs, APKWS guided rockets and ATAS missiles. It lacks an attack helicopter's armour and built-in gun. It arrived in the "Kings of Battle" update.
mi_24a: Developed in the late 1960s and in service from 1972, the Mi-24A 'Hind-A' combined gunship and troop transport roles, carrying a 12.7 mm nose gun, rockets and anti-tank missiles while also handling casualty evacuation and troop insertion; Hinds in later forms remain in service. As the second Soviet helicopter in the game, it carries much the same weapons as the Mi-4AV but is over 100 km/h faster with 400 hp more, which allows hit-and-run attacks with its ATGMs, rockets and A-12.7 gun instead of hovering. Its light armour makes enemy SPAA a constant danger. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
mi_24d: Designed in 1973 as the dedicated gunship Hind, the Mi-24D replaced the A's single cockpit with separate positions for pilot and gunner and gained fire control for 57 mm rocket pods, UPK-23 gun pods and Falanga ATGMs; widely exported, it served Czechoslovakia and then the Czech Republic until most went to Ukraine in 2023. In the game it is versatile in attack and support roles, with twin TV3-117V engines giving good lift and handling for its weight, a wide-arc 12.7 mm turret and varied ordnance. Its armour resists machine guns and light cannon. Sold as a pack from Update 1.81, it left the store after the 2019 New Year Sale.
mi_24d_german: Early Mi-24 service exposed a poor cockpit layout and a weak A-12.7 gun, so the Mi-24D gained tandem cockpits and a four-barrel 12.7 mm YakB in a remote chin turret, entering service in 1976 without the delayed Shturm-V missiles. East Germany received 42 between 1978 and 1984, mainly for border areas, and the Bundeswehr kept them briefly after reunification before selling them from 1993. In the game it can carry full S-5K rocket pods, 250 or 500 kg bombs for risky strikes, or Falanga ATGMs for stand-off attacks. Its 12-tonne weight hurts handling, partly offset by good speed. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
mi_24d_hungary: Hungary's Cold War air arm concentrated on air defence, so its first Mi-24s arrived only in 1993, when Germany gave it 20 Mi-24D/Vs inherited from East Germany. The D, in production from 1973, was the first major Hind upgrade, a true gunship with a four-barrel 12.7 mm Yak-B, 57 mm rocket pods and Falanga missiles. In the game it is a capable multirole helicopter, fast but less agile than lighter types like the AH-1. Falanga ATGMs, S-24 rockets and a ballistic computer are strong, the 12.7 mm gun less so; cannon SPAA such as the Gepard is a serious threat, though countermeasures help. It came in "Sons of Attila".
mi_24p: Created in 1981 as an anti-armour Mi-24V, the Mi-24P 'Hind-F' swapped the gunner's 12.7 mm chin turret for a fixed, pilot-aimed GSh-30-2K twin 30 mm cannon taken from the Su-25, and it was exported widely alongside the V. In the game it is otherwise identical to the Mi-24V in airframe, systems and weapons. The fixed cannon is awkward to aim, but a short burst tears through lightly armoured vehicles, making the P a sidegrade that trades some anti-infantry flexibility for anti-armour punch. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
mi_24p_german: East Germany's first Mi-24Ps arrived in 1982 to join its Mi-24Ds on border patrol; after reunification they passed to the Bundeswehr, where a few were tested, two went to the USA, and most were later sold to Poland and Hungary. In the game it is a true multi-role helicopter: 9M114 Shturm ATGMs hit tanks from beyond the reach of many air defences, while all-aspect R-60M missiles and the 30 mm GSh-30-2K handle aircraft. High top speed helps attack runs, but its 12 tonnes blunt manoeuvrability, and the fixed cannon is tricky against close air targets. It came in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
mi_24p_german_hfs80: Among the very few ex-East German types the Bundeswehr kept flying, the Mi-24P served for four years until the Tiger took over anti-tank duties; survivors went to Hungary or to WTD-61 for testing. One of the last, from Heeresfliegerstaffel 80, received a farewell livery before being sold to Hungary in 1995. This premium carries that scheme and otherwise plays exactly like other Mi-24Ps. Its size and heavy controls make it an easy target, but the powerful 30 mm gun, decent armour and good survivability still reward an aggressive approach. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mi_24p_hungary: Hungary found the 20 Mi-24D/Vs gifted by Germany in 1993 already outdated, so an upgrade programme brought them towards V and P standard with the fixed GSh-30-2 twin cannon, 9K114 Shturm radio-guided missiles, integrated navigation and communications, and English-language displays. In the game it shares the Mi-24V's airframe, systems and weapons, except that the chin Yak-B Gatling gives way to the fixed 30 mm cannon on the right of the nose. Hard to aim but able to shred light vehicles with a short burst, it trades a little anti-air ability for more ground-attack punch. It came in "Sons of Attila".
mi_24v: In 1976 the Mi-24D was modernised with 9M114 Shturm missiles, which outranged the Falanga, guided better and were small enough to carry twice as many, plus a new fire-control system; the result, the Mi-24V, became the most produced Hind with over 1,500 built. In the game the 'Hind-E' pairs the tandem bubble canopies with a chin 12.7 mm Gatling and a choice of 57 mm pods, S-24 rockets, Shturms, bombs, gun pods and all-aspect R-60M missiles. Exhaust suppressors, IR jamming and flares improve survivability, making it one of the best-equipped helicopters at its rank. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
mi_24v_hungary: Similar to the Mi-24D flown across the Warsaw Pact, the Mi-24V of 1976 added the 9M114 Shturm missile, eight of which fit on the outer pylons, and with some 1,500 built it was the most numerous Hind. Hungary began flying it in 1993 among the 20 Mi-24D/Vs donated by Germany. In the game the Shturm makes it a big step up from the Mi-24D, and it is fast enough to reach objectives quickly, though very clumsy beside other helicopters. Countermeasures help, but the 12.7 mm gun in place of a cannon struggles at close range, especially in arcade battles. It came in "Sons of Attila".
mi_28a_sweden: In 1995 Sweden's army chief Åke Sagrén called for a dedicated attack helicopter, and the AH-64 and Mi-28A were trialled with Swedish crews as gunners; the Apache proved effective but complex, the Havoc reliable, easy to fly and easier to maintain, but budget cuts and changing priorities cancelled the purchase. In the game this early-production Mi-28A has fewer loadouts and less sophisticated sights than the Mi-28N and NM but remains very dangerous. Its rockets and 30 mm gun make it a strong early-spawn helicopter, while Ataka missiles keep it useful at range later in a match. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
mi_28n: The Mi-28N 'Havoc' was developed to overcome the Mi-24's limits, dropping the troop cabin to become a pure attack helicopter, and entered Russian service in 2009; it keeps Mil's traditions of heavy weight, strong armour for a helicopter and blunt looks, but feels less bulky to fly. In the game its ordnance largely mirrors the Mi-35M, with Ataka ATGMs, rockets and Igla missiles, though it carries twice as many ATGMs. Its standout feature is a chin-mounted 30 mm 2A42 from the BMP-2, with wide arcs, APDS rounds and an auto-tracker, which rewards bold close-range attacks. It came in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
mi_28nm: The Mi-28NM is Rostvertol's upgraded Havoc, with the N025 radar, improved avionics and optics, more powerful VK-2500 engines and new weapons; it first flew in 2016, passed state trials in 2020, and the Mi-28N fleet is due to be brought up to the same standard. In the game it adds third-generation gunner thermals, radar, missile approach warning and a new RWR, plus Vikhr laser-guided and radar-guided Khrizantema ATGMs. It is less flexible than its Kamov rivals but devastating against tanks thanks to precise weapons, strong survivability, good handling and capable sensors. It arrived in the "Ground Breaking" update.
mi_35m: Short of money to replace its Hinds with Mi-28s and Ka-50s, post-Soviet Russia modernised them as the Mi-35M, with a glass cockpit, fire-control computers, satellite navigation, the GOES-342 thermal sight, Ataka ATGMs, Igla missiles, a GSh-23-2 turret in place of the 12.7 mm gun and the Vitebsk defensive suite; over 60 were in service by 2018. In the game the 'Super Hind' brings top-tier systems to the familiar Mi-24 airframe, so experienced Hind pilots can concentrate on the new equipment. Its guided weapons and sensors make it a far stronger tank hunter, well able to support Soviet MBTs. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
mi_35m_pakistan: Pakistan began looking to replace its AH-1Fs in 2010, but with candidates such as the Z-10, AH-1Z, AH-64D and T129 caught up in political delays, it ordered four Mi-35Ms in 2015 as a stopgap, its first arms deal with Russia; they entered service in 2018. In the game it matches the Russian version apart from desert camouflage, offering varied guided and unguided weapons, plus a cannon and Igla missiles against aircraft. Its weapons' short range keeps it within reach of SAMs, it handles heavily, especially at speed, and its RWR warns of radar locks but not lasers or fire-and-forget missiles. It came in "Firebirds".
mi_35p: Unveiled at Army-2018 and in Russian service from 2020, the Mi-35P updates the Mi-24P while keeping its long wings and retractable undercarriage, adding Ataka and Vikhr missiles and borrowing the Mi-35M's movable 23 mm GSh-23L turret in place of the fixed 30 mm cannon. In the game it improves on the Mi-35M with a newer radar warning receiver and countermeasures and can carry up to 16 Ataka or Vikhr missiles, though not alongside a full load of air-to-air missiles. Its sheer size makes it an easy mark for anti-aircraft guns and fighters. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
mi_35p_indonesia: Indonesia chose the Mi-35P, the export Mi-24P, as its first dedicated attack helicopter for counter-insurgency in remote jungle, valuing its mix of heavy weapons and troop space; the purchase also strengthened ties with Russia during Western arms embargoes after East Timor, and deliveries ran from 2003 to 2010. In the Japanese tree, it performs exactly like the Soviet Mi-24P, with the same starboard GSh-30-2K cannon, Shturm missiles, R-60s, rockets, bombs and gun pods. Its engines are slightly stronger, but 80 extra horsepower makes barely any difference. It arrived in the "Tusk Force" update.
mi_4av: The Mi-4 answered the American H-19 and was rushed into service in 1953, earning a reputation for reliability and payload; the armed Mi-4AV of 1966 tested the Mi-24A's weapon system, with up to four Falanga ATGMs, rocket pods or bombs and a 12.7 mm gun in a ventral gondola, and around 200 were converted. In the game the Soviet starter helicopter seems weak at first, underpowered and sluggish, especially fully loaded, and an easy target for radar SPAA. Yet its four Falangas reach 4 km, further than any other starter helicopter's missiles and beyond many SPAA. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
mi_8amtsh: Developed at Ulan-Ude in 1996 from the Mi-8AMT transport, the Mi-8AMTSh assault version gained guided weapons like those of modern Mi-24s, including the 9M114 Shturm, plus extra armour, new avionics and design changes, and entered Russian Air Force service in 2009. In the game its longer-ranged Shturms replace the Falanga, alongside Igla missiles, new gun pods and flares against IR missiles. It is still huge and heavy, however, so weaving between trees and terrain is impractical and dodging missiles is hard. It came in the "Kings of Battle" update.
mi_8amtsh_vn: The Mi-8AMTSh-VN "Sapsan" drew on combat experience in Syria and elsewhere, gaining new engines, a composite four-blade rotor similar to the Mi-28's, an improved cabin and electronics for Ataka and Verba missiles, plus better survivability and controls; shown at MAKS 2017, ten were ordered in 2019 for delivery by 2022. In the game Ataka missiles and a thermal imager let it strike from much further away, and improved protective systems sharpen awareness. It is still as large and heavy as any Mi-8, though. It arrived in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
mi_8tb: The Mi-8TB was the export version of the Mi-8TV, developed in 1968 with 9M14M Malyutka missiles in place of the Falanga. East Germany received over 100 Mi-8s of various models, and a few outdated TBs were still flying at reunification because the Soviet withdrawal halted their replacement; the last left German service in 1992. In the game its sole change from the Mi-8TV is six Malyutkas in place of four Falangas, so it is otherwise the same, with room for many rocket pods and bombs, but its great size and weight rule out weaving through terrain, so dodging fire is difficult. It came in "Sons of Attila".
mi_8tv: Mikhail Mil sold the Mi-8 to a sceptical Soviet government as a mere turbine-powered Mi-4, until Khrushchev, impressed by a 1959 flight in the US presidential S-58, ordered a comparable helicopter; the twin-turbine V-8 became a worldwide success, and the armed Mi-8TV followed for troop support. In the game the 'Hip' is a big step up from the Mi-4AV and a reasonable alternative to the early Mi-24A, with ATGMs, rockets, bombs and rare incendiary bombs. It flies far better than the Mi-4, but it is no Cobra: its bulk makes it an easy target for SPAA at close range. It came in "Sons of Attila".
mig-15: The MiG-15bis replaced the original MiG-15's RD-45, a copied Rolls-Royce Nene with quality and reliability problems, with the home-grown VK-1, which had a larger combustion chamber and turbine; the extra power improved dogfighting and allowed heavier ground ordnance. Among the first jets to head the Soviet tree, present since before the open beta, it now teaches the energy management and trigger discipline later Soviet jets demand. Its strong engine and guns let it outperform most jets it meets, though missiles call for vigilance and ammunition is limited. In uptiers it can hang back, picking off distracted enemies and even out-turning some supersonic jets.
mig-15_ns23: After Britain sold the Soviets Nene and Derwent engines along with production licences, Mikoyan's I-310, with a 35-degree swept wing and a single RD-45, beat Yakovlev's delayed Yak-30 to become the MiG-15, which served widely and was built abroad as the Lim-1, S-102 and J-2. Introduced in Update 1.35 as the Soviet answer to the F-86F-25, the 'Fagot' has above-average energy performance and hard-hitting but scarce ammunition, with a very poor roll rate. It is an energy fighter at heart but can turn with some opponents when needed, and it leads on to the stronger-engined MiG-15bis.
mig-15bis_ish: In 1953–54 the MiG-15bis was adapted for several new roles, and the ISh was a ground-attack 'Shturmovik' version with long wing-fence pylons and experimental downward-angled rocket rails, allowing a big bomb load for a MiG-15 or many rockets. In the game it is arguably the strongest Soviet MiG-15, combining plenty of strike ordnance with the bis's powerful engine, easily compensating for the drag of its oversized pylons. Sold as a pack from Update 1.85 "Supersonic", it was withdrawn after the 2019 Birthday sale, appeared in occasional events and became permanently available for Golden Eagles in 2023.
mig-15bis_nr23_china: China's J-2 is the MiG-15bis as flown by Chinese forces in the Korean War, defending the mainland from American bombers and intercepting aircraft over North Korea; despite losses, some Chinese pilots downed enemy aces or became aces themselves, and the type served another decade until licence-built J-5s replaced it in the 1960s. It performs exactly like the Soviet MiG-15bis, its VK-1 engine and heavy guns giving it an edge over earlier jets, though missiles and limited ammunition need watching. It can also double as an improvised attacker while still able to fight some supersonic jets. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mig-15bis_nr23_german: East Germany received the VK-1-powered MiG-15bis soon after it had proved itself in Soviet service, and it served as the NVA's frontline fighter, later joined by MiG-17s and Polish Lim-5s, until third-generation types such as the MiG-21F replaced it around 1970. In the game it is identical to the Soviet MiG-15bis: a strong engine and powerful guns give it the upper hand over most jets it meets, provided its pilot watches for missiles and rations ammunition. In uptiers it works best supporting from behind, picking off enemies who are distracted and holding its own against some supersonic jets in close fights. It came in Update 1.39.
mig-15bis_nr23_hungary: Hungary was a major MiG-15bis user and part of the Soviet bloc's interceptor screen, regularly scrambling against NATO aircraft probing its airspace; on 19 November 1951 a MiG-15bis flown by 1st Lt A. A. Kalugin forced a straying USAF C-47 to land at Pápa. The type served until the MiG-17 and MiG-21 took over. In the Hungarian part of the Italian tree, it matches the Soviet and German versions exactly: strong engine and guns and a small, agile airframe that dogfights superbly for its size, but limited ammunition and vulnerability to missiles. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
mig-17: Begun as the MiG-15bis-45, the MiG-17 cured the MiG-15's violent buffeting and loss of control near Mach 1 with a new wing, airfoil and tailplane, becoming one of the most successful transonic fighters; in Vietnam its agility, small size and guns let it beat far newer F-4s and F-105s. In the game it barely improves on the MiG-15 in speed, energy or turning, but its compression limit is much higher, allowing faster combat manoeuvres. Uptiers bring all-aspect AIM-9L and R-60M carriers such as the A-10A and Su-25, which are deadly to it. It came in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
mig-17_china: The J-4 represents MiG-17s supplied by the USSR before licence production as the J-5: drawings, two aircraft and kits arrived in 1955, and the first Chinese-assembled jet flew on 19 July 1956. It scored victories over the Nationalists in the Taiwan Strait Crisis, though on 24 September 1958 one became the first aircraft ever lost to an air-to-air missile, an AIM-9B. In the game it performs like the Soviet MiG-17; it is best fought at lower speeds, as its controls are not built for over 900 km/h, and its heavy guns kill quickly, but AIM-9B or R-3S-armed opponents demand constant awareness. It came with the Chinese tree in Update 1.91.
mig-17_cuba: Cuba bought the MiG-17AS in 1964 to replace its MiG-15bis, gaining a more reliable engine and wiring for R-3S missiles, and flew it until MiG-23s took over in the 1980s. On 5 October 1969 Lt Eduardo Guerra Jimenez defected in aircraft number 232, landing undetected at Homestead AFB in Florida while Air Force One was on the base, which triggered major US security reforms. In the game it shares the tech-tree MiG-17's strengths and weaknesses, the only real difference being R-3S missiles, so it is mainly a collector's aircraft. Sold as a pack from Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it left the store after the 2022 May sale.
mig-17_f5: Shenyang's F-5 stands for the Chinese-built J-5s, licensed MiG-17Fs, given to North Korea as military aid; Factory 112 received the licence in 1953, the first J-5 flew on 19 July 1956, and the type went on to score victories against Taiwanese and American aircraft. In the game it is an improved MiG-17F with an afterburning VK-1F (WP-5), heavy cannons and two PL-2 missiles, so pilots familiar with earlier MiGs will adapt quickly. It handles most subsonic jets well, but against early supersonic fighters it should wait until they have lost energy. A premium pack from Update 1.91, it later returned for Golden Eagles in 2022.
mig-17p_lim_5p: Poland licence-built the MiG-17 as the Lim-5 from 1955, and the Lim-5P of 1956 copied the MiG-17PF with an afterburning VK-1 and RP-5 Izumrud radar; 129 were made, and Lim-5s, cheaper than Soviet originals, were widely exported, with ex-German Lim-5Ps flying in Guinea-Bissau until 2011. In the game it stands apart from other MiG-17s: three 23 mm cannons replace the mixed 37 mm and 23 mm armament, making gunnery much easier, and it has the afterburning VK-1F. Its RP-5 radar, like the MiG-19PT's, uses separate search and track antennas for an early form of track-while-scan. It came in "Danger Zone".
mig-17pf_hungary: Overtaken by the MiG-19 and MiG-21, the MiG-17 was kept useful as a rear-line interceptor by the MiG-17PF upgrade, which combined the F's afterburning VK-1 with the P's RP-5 Izumrud radar and simplified the guns to three NR-23s. Widely exported, it served in Hungary, and museum aircraft Red 401 is almost identical to the in-game Red 403. In the game it plays more aggressively than the Soviet MiG-17, with more thrust and easier gunnery, but the extra weight raises wing loading and makes high-speed control lock-up more pronounced. Advanced missiles and supersonic fighters in uptiers are a serious threat. It came in "Alpha Strike".
mig-19j_6a: Conceived as a mass-produced, expendable fighter, the J-6 began in 1958 as a MiG-19P copy, the first supersonic fighter anywhere in East or Southeast Asia, though poor quality halted that version after 83; a J-6 later downed an F-104 in 1965. The J-6A returned to production from 1975 as the 'New A' with PL-2 missiles, 173 being built by 1983. In the game it flies just like the MiG-19PT: huge acceleration and firepower beat subsonic jets, though it compresses badly at transonic speed. Lured into dogfights, MiG-21s and Phantoms fall quickly to its 30 mm cannons. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mig-19pt: Designed in the early 1950s, the MiG-19 'Farmer' was the first Soviet aircraft to fly supersonic in level flight, a fast and fairly agile interceptor best remembered for Vietnam; the MiG-19PT was a single MiG-19P adapted to carry R-3S 'Atoll' missiles. In the game it arrived as one of the first three missile-armed jets, together with the F-100D and Javelin FAW Mk 9. Its speed and manoeuvrability let it win many energy fights, but it has no countermeasures, so careful watch for enemy missiles is vital. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
mig-19s: The MiG-19S introduced an all-moving tailplane, the Svod navigation receiver and three 30 mm NR-30 cannons instead of two; production began in 1956, and East Germany flew 12 alongside 12 MiG-19PMs until MiG-21s replaced them in 1969. In the game it is the German counterpart to the MiG-19PT, lacking missiles and a search and track radar but lighter for it and carrying an extra gun with more ammunition, so in skilled hands it is at least a sidegrade. It makes a strong introduction to supersonic jets, teaching missile evasion and higher-tier dogfighting that the F-104G does not. It came in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
mig-21_bis: Developed from 1972 around the Tumansky R-25, which could give a lightened MiG-21 a thrust-to-weight ratio above 1 on full afterburner, the MiG-21bis was the final third-generation Fishbed, built in Lazur-M and SAU versions that differed mainly in guidance and landing systems. In the game it resembles the MiG-21S and MF outwardly, with radar, a GSh-23 and a deep spine, but its R-25-300 engine adds thrust and its fire control allows R-13M1 missiles and twin-rail pylons carrying double the R-60Ms. Short of strong long-range missiles, it excels in close, low-altitude dogfights against most opponents. It came in the "New Power" update.
mig-21_bis_lazur: East Germany received 46 MiG-21bis from the mid-1970s to replace older MF and PFM models: 14 'Fishbed-L' aircraft with the Lazur-M ground-controlled intercept system, named MiG-21bis Lazur-M, and 32 'Fishbed-N' with Polyot-OI, the bis-SAU. In the game it is virtually identical to the tech-tree MiG-21bis-SAU, since the guidance system has no effect on play. It strikes hard and fast against unaware targets and punishes anyone who dogfights it at speed, relying on flight performance and strong acceleration rather than its radar, avionics and missiles, which lag behind its rivals. It came in "Apex Predators".
mig-21_bis_sau: The bis-SAU was the Polyot-OI-equipped 'Fishbed-N' version of the MiG-21bis, 32 of which made up most of East Germany's 46 from the 1970s, told apart from the Lazur-M model only by one antenna under the nose. In the game it extends the MiG-21MF's style: superb flight performance for hit-and-run attacks and for dogfighting out of trouble, with a powerful engine to regain the speed its delta wing sheds. Its systems are the weak point, with one of the poorest radars at its rank, mediocre missiles, no BVR capability and the basic SPO-10 RWR, so it demands skill but rewards mastery. It came in "Ground Breaking".
mig-21_bis_sau_hungary: Hungary received 63 MiG-21bis from 1977, 39 with Lazur-M and 24 Polyot-equipped bis-SAUs; the latter lacked wiring for internal ASO-2 flare dispensers and needed an external SPS-141 pod. In the Hungarian branch of the Italian tree, it plays like other late Fishbeds: excellent performance and a strong engine for hit-and-run attacks and close dogfights, but terrible energy retention and weak systems, with a poor radar, no BVR missiles, the outdated SPO-10 RWR and missiles outclassed by IRCCM-equipped rivals. The countermeasure pod adds a barely noticeable penalty compared with Lazur versions. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
mig-21_bison: India's MiG-21 Bison came from a 1990s upgrade of its MiG-21bis fleet, based on the MiG-21-93 package with kits produced by HAL with Mikoyan's help, omitting some features while adding Indian systems such as the TARANG warning and jamming suite; all IAF MiG-21s were retired in 2024. As a British premium it offers an alternative to the F-4J UK for research. Its weapons and avionics are excellent for its rank, but missile count and flight performance show their limits against F-15s, Su-27s and JAS-39s. A rare ground-tracking radar mode and KAB-500Kr TV-guided bombs enable precise strikes, though ordnance and countermeasures are scarce. It came in "Seek & Destroy".
mig-21_f13: When a dud AIM-9B lodged in a Chinese MiG-17 in September 1958, the Soviets reverse-engineered it as the K-13, and the MiG-21F-13 gave up one cannon to carry it. In the game it breaks with the MiG-15, 17 and 19 that precede it: instead of strong low-speed energy retention, it has poor energy retention and low-speed agility but superb angle of attack and instantaneous turning at speed. Weak missiles and a single low-velocity gun with only 60 rounds call for caution, so it does best staying clear of the main fight and picking off distracted targets with hit-and-run passes. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mig-21_mf: East Germany replaced its MiG-21F-13s with newer variants from the late 1960s, chief among them the MiG-21MF ('Modernised, Uprated'), with a new radar, more fuel, an uprated engine and R-60 missiles; it formed the backbone of the air force until the MiG-21bis and MiG-23MF arrived. In the game its built-in GSh-23 means countermeasures need not cost it the gun, and R-60s give it a strong arsenal for its rank, matched by excellent high-speed manoeuvrability. It is lighter than the Soviet MiG-21SMT, but the SMT's far stronger engine wins evenly matched dogfights. It came in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
mig-21_mf_hungary: The MiG-21 earned a grim reputation in Hungary, where faulty engines, inadequate training and poor maintenance led to 72 airframes and 32 pilots lost in accidents; Hungary acquired 50 MiG-21MFs between 1971 and 1974 and retired the last in 1996. In the game its internal GSh-23 means the SPS-141 countermeasure pod does not cost it a cannon, and R-60 missiles plus excellent high-speed handling make it a dangerous fighter. It is lighter than the Soviet MiG-21SMT but loses to the SMT's stronger engine in long, even fights. It adds welcome variety to the Italian tree's Hungarian branch and arrived in "Alpha Strike".
mig-21_pfm: The MiG-21, built in over 11,000 examples, more than any other supersonic aircraft, replaced the Soviet Union's subsonic fighters, and the PF series added radar and avionics for all-weather interception. The PFM refined it further, but with no internal gun it relied on a GP-9 belly pod and external weapons. In the game it plays much like the MiG-21F-13 despite its RP-21M radar and 23 mm GSh-23L pod. It is strongest at high altitude, accelerating quickly and handling well, which suits boom-and-zoom, and Kh-66 missiles allow light ground attack from range. It was a reward in the 2020 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. event.
mig-21_s: Wanting a better air-to-air fighter than the MiG-21PF, the Soviet Air Force adopted the MiG-21S, combining the Ye-7S prototype's Sapfir-21 radar, radar-computing gunsight and R-3R semi-active missiles with the MiG-21R's larger saddle tank; deliveries began in 1965, and it took part in the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia. In the game it is in effect a MiG-21PFM on the MiG-21R airframe, gaining fuel and hardpoints. Superb flight performance and R-3R missiles, useful head-on or from the side against unwary targets, are its strengths, but with no countermeasures it is very exposed to AIM-9Ls and R-60Ms. It was a Golden Eagles premium from "Winged Lions".
mig-21_smt: To fix the MiG-21's short range, the SMT added a huge saddle tank, an upgraded Sapfir radar able to fire R-3R and R-60 missiles, and a much stronger engine, but pilots disliked the heavy 'Hunchback', and from 1972 all were rebuilt as the MiG-21ST with the smaller tank of the bis. In the game it is the first Soviet fighter with countermeasures and brings R-3R and R-60 missiles, while its engine gives quick acceleration and high top speed. It bleeds energy in almost any manoeuvre but regains it fast when flying straight, a pattern that shapes later Soviet jets. It came in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
mig-21_sps_k: East German naming got tangled when Soviet MiG-21PFMs arrived alongside locally modified PFs already called PFM, so the Soviet aircraft became the MiG-21SPS, and the later version able to carry a GSh-23 belly pod became the SPS-K, for Kanone. In the game it departs from the usual Fishbed approach: with no built-in gun it relies on R-60, R-13M1 and R-3R missiles, but only two hardpoints limit it to four, and the centre pylon takes either a gun pod or an SPS-141 countermeasure pod. Flight performance remains very good. A premium pack from "Ground Breaking", it left the store after the 2023 May Sale.
mig-9: Built after the capture of German jet technology in 1945, Mikoyan's I-300 was a pod-and-boom twin-jet with two RD-20s, copies of the BMW 003; a coin toss with the Yak-15 team let it fly first, making it the first Soviet jet in the air. The 57 mm version was dropped, partly because its gun gases caused engine flameouts, so the MiG-9 entered production with a 37 mm and two 23 mm cannons. In the game it suffers awful acceleration, mediocre agility and low-velocity guns with little ammunition, but excels at boom-and-zoom, using speed and hard-hitting guns from above. It has been in the game since the open beta.
mig-9_china: The MiG-9 was the first jet to reach China, joining the air force in 1950 as Soviet units transferred aircraft and China bought more to defend its cities against Nationalist bombers ahead of the Korean War. Adequate against F-80s and F-84Bs but outclassed once F-86s appeared, it became a lead-in trainer after the MiG-15 arrived and was retired in 1959. In the game it performs like the Soviet MiG-9: small, nimble and hard-hitting, but its weak early engine and awkward ballistics take practice, and losing speed carelessly can see it shot down by propeller fighters. It came with the first Chinese air tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mig-9_late_china: Alongside the earlier version, this later MiG-9 formed China's first jet force from 1950, provided by the Soviet Union and supplemented by purchases to protect major cities from Nationalist raids; it held its own against F-80s and F-84Bs but gave way to MiG-15s and ended as a jet trainer until 1959. In the game it matches the Soviet MiG-9 (l), whose new engine with a WEP mode improves acceleration. Even so, speed management remains vital, and unexpected third parties in a dogfight are dangerous, as a slow MiG-9 is easy prey even for propeller aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mig-9_ussr: In 1947 Mikoyan fitted two MiG-9s with experimental RD-20F engines that had a forced-reheat mode, an early form of afterburner; the engine proved unreliable, and the pair were designated I-307, represented in the game as the MiG-9 (l). Compared with the standard MiG-9 it adds underwing fuel pods and RD-20F engines with more power and WEP, fixing much of the original's sluggish acceleration. It still plays as a boom-and-zoom fighter, now doing the job far better, but second-generation jets in uptiers can beat it with ease. It has been in the game since the open beta.
mig_21_2000_iaf: IAI's MiG-21-2000 was a 1990s package to modernise the MiG-21bis with entirely new avionics; a 1993 deal with Romania, where Aerostar installed IAI and Elbit kits on around 100 aircraft, surprised Russia, which had been courting the same customers. It added an Elta EL/M-2032 pulse-Doppler radar, multifunction displays, a helmet-mounted sight and Western weapons led by the Python 3. In the game the radar spots enemies earlier, and all-aspect Python 3 missiles make it deadly in close fights. It accelerates and turns very well at subsonic speed like the MiG-21bis, but limited fuel and a fragile airframe demand discipline. It came in Update 2.57.
mig_21_bis_finland: The MiG-21's first customer from outside the Warsaw Pact, Finland started with F-13s in 1963 and in 1977 acquired 26 MiG-21bis of the Polyot-equipped 'Fishbed-N' type, flying them until F/A-18C Hornets replaced them in 1998. In the Swedish tree it is identical to the Soviet MiG-21bis apart from camouflage and export missile names such as the R-60MK. It plays the same way, exploiting outstanding angle of attack, instantaneous turning and acceleration, while poor energy retention and missiles weaker than many opponents' call for care. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
mig_23bn: The MiG-23BN improved the MiG-23B ground-attack Flogger with the MiG-23ML's Type 3 wing and an upgraded R-29 engine; little used by the Soviets, it was popular for export, and East Germany received 18 in the late 1970s, without dielectric fairings or countermeasure dispensers, flying them alongside its Su-22s. In the game it has no countermeasures, guided weapons or air-to-air missiles, yet it is fast and versatile, and with gun pods and the ability to outrun most enemies it works surprisingly well as a fighter. In mixed battles its ballistic computer and CCIP make bombs, rockets and S-24B rockets accurate. It came in "Drone Age".
mig_23m: Designed to stop low-flying nuclear strike jets that the MiG-21 could not, the MiG-23 needed a look-down radar, strong missiles and short-field ability; the swing-wing MiG-23-02 beat a lift-jet delta, entering service in 1970 as the MiG-23S, and the MiG-23M with Sapfir-23D radar, TP-23 IRST and R-23R and R-23T missiles followed as the first true production model. In the game it relies on systems rather than performance: the first Soviet fighter with medium-range radar missiles, it has a look-down radar, variable-sweep wings and IRST. Its wings break if pushed too hard and countermeasures are scarce. It came in "Red Skies".
mig_23mf_germany: The MiG-23MF was the export version of the MiG-23M, built as the 23-11A for Warsaw Pact customers without nuclear delivery systems, and a further downgraded 23-11B for other countries. In the game it is essentially identical to the Soviet MiG-23M, with strong weapons and good dogfighting thanks to its swing wings, but very poor survivability from a tiny countermeasure supply and an outdated RWR. It bridges the gap from the MiG-21bis-SAU, although the German tree's own MiG-23MLA is better. It was a reward in the 2021 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. event during the "Winged Lions" update.
mig_23mf_hungary: Hungary received 12 MiG-23MFs, the export MiG-23M, and flew them until 1997, when it sought NATO-compatible aircraft and ultimately the Gripen. The MF came in a Warsaw Pact version without nuclear delivery equipment and a more downgraded one for other customers. In the Hungarian branch of the Italian tree, it plays like the Soviet MiG-23M and the German event MF, combining strong missiles and agile variable-sweep wings with poor survivability due to scarce countermeasures and an old RWR. It offers an alternative to the MiG-21bis-SAU, relying more on missiles and avionics than flight performance. It came in "Alpha Strike".
mig_23ml: Early MiG-23s had many flaws, so the MiG-23ML ('lightweight') of the 1970s shed weight and drag by deleting a fuselage tank, trimming the dorsal fin and fitting a lighter, sturdier undercarriage and wing-sweep mechanism, and added the R-25F-300 engine, Sapfir-23ML radar and a TP-23M IRST with up to twice the range, plus BDS-50-60 flare dispensers, R-24 missiles and UPK-23 gun pods. In the game this pack premium is functionally the same as the German MiG-23MLA and close to the MiG-23MLD: powerful and versatile, with a radar that, paired with R-24R and R-24T missiles, is lethal beyond visual range. It came in "Apex Predators".
mig_23mla: The MiG-23MLA was the export MiG-23ML with an improved N-003 radar offering more range and ECCM, and it was the first export Flogger with the TP-23M IRST and clearance for R-24R and R-24T missiles; East Germany received 28. In the game it is identical to the MiG-23ML, with BDS-50-60 flares and R-24s setting it apart from the MiG-23M and MF. It wins mainly through its weapons and avionics but can dogfight less agile opponents. As the German counterpart of the MiG-23MLD, it bridges the MiG-21bis-SAU and MiG-29, teaching target priority and missile use. It came in "Wind of Change".
mig_23mld: The MiG-23MLD was the final Flogger, ordered in the early 1980s as a stopgap until MiG-29 teething troubles were solved: a lighter airframe, strengthened 'Type 4' dogtooth wings with new slats and vortex generators, the R-35F-300 engine, N-008 radar and the MiG-29's SPO-15L RWR. Most were rebuilt from MLs and MLAs, and in skilled hands they could beat MiG-29s. In the game it out-turns almost every third-generation fighter and some heavier fourth-generation ones, carries plenty of R-60Ms plus R-24R/T missiles, radar and IRST, and has six times the flares of the MiG-23M. It came in "Ground Breaking".
mig_25pd: Designed to counter fast bombers like the B-58 and the projected XB-70 and SR-71, Mikoyan's E-155P first flew in September 1964 and entered service as the MiG-25P in 1972. After Viktor Belenko flew one to Japan in 1976, the upgraded PD followed from 1978 with the Sapfir-25 radar and stronger R15BD-300 engines, serving Soviet air defence into the early 1990s and abroad, notably in the Iran–Iraq War. In the game it climbs and accelerates superbly, and long-range R-40RD and R-40TD missiles are its weapons. It has no gun, handles poorly and is restricted by airspeed limits at low altitude. It was a 2025 "Winter Concert" event reward.
